value.zh: 故有避於言色，其道聞乎孔公；
value.en: Hence men who gave nothing away in word or look, whose path we know because Confucius spoke of them;
value.literal: Therefore there were those who avoided it in speech and countenance; of their way one hears from the Duke Kong;

value.zh: 驕乎富貴，厥義詳于孫子。
value.en: and the proud scorning of wealth and station, whose moral sense Sunzi laid out at length.
value.literal: As for pride toward wealth and noble rank, its meaning was set forth in detail by Master Sun.

value.zh: 是以處柔伊存，有生之恆性；
value.en: To hold to yielding strength is how life endures; that is the fixed temper of everything that breathes;
value.literal: Therefore to abide in softness is how it endures; it is the constant nature of the living;

value.zh: 在盈斯害，惟神之常道。
value.en: while fullness invites injury—such has always been heaven's steady law.
value.literal: to be at fullness is thereby harm; it is the constant way of the spirit.

value.zh: 古先智士體其若茲，介焉超俗，浩然養素，藏聲江海之上，卷跡囂氛之表，漱流而激其清，寢巢而韜其耀，良畫以符其志，絕機以虛其心。
value.en: Men of old who grasped this truth stood aloof from the crowd, breathed in a clarity that nourished plain living, let their names die away beyond the rivers and seas, and withdrew their footsteps from the world's noise. They drank from running water to keep themselves clean, dwelt like birds in the wild to dim their luster, chose their course with deliberate care, and stilled every scheme so the heart could rest empty.
value.literal: Ancient wise men embodied it thus: standing apart they transcended the vulgar, in vast purity they nurtured simplicity, they hid their voices above the rivers and seas, they rolled up their traces beyond the clamor and dust, they rinsed their mouths in the current to quicken its clearness, they slept in nests to sheathe their brilliance, they took fine plans to match their intent, they cut off contrivance to empty their hearts.

value.zh: 玉輝冰潔，川渟岳峙，修至樂之道，固無疆之休，長往邈而不追，安排窅而無悶，修身自保，悔吝弗生，詩人《考槃》之歌，抑在茲矣。
value.en: They shone like jade and held the chill of ice; they were still as a held river, steadfast as a mountain. They walked the path of deepest contentment and won a peace without end. Once they had gone far, none could overtake them; they accepted whatever came, untroubled in the dark. Guarding the person, they kept harm away—no cause for remorse—and the ode the Classic of Poetry calls "Kao pan" might almost have been written of them.
value.literal: Jade radiance, ice purity; like a river at rest, like a peak standing; they cultivated the way of supreme joy, they secured boundless good fortune; long gone, remote, none could pursue them; settled in the depths, without vexation; they cultivated the self to preserve themselves, regret and shame did not arise—the poet's song of "Kao pan," is it not here?

value.zh: 至於體天作制之後，訟息刑清之時，尚乃仄席幽貞以康神化，徵聘之禮賁於岩穴，玉帛之贄委於窒衡，故《月令》曰：「季春之月聘名士，禮賢者」，斯之謂歟！
value.en: Even once a ruler had aligned his government with heaven and the courts fell quiet, he would still leave the high seat half-empty for recluses of firm integrity, so culture might flourish. Envoys climbed to mountain huts; jade and silk waited on the doorsteps of the poor. That is why the "Monthly Ordinances" says that in late spring one should call forth noted scholars and honor the wise—surely it speaks of just such a time.
value.literal: As for after one embodied heaven and established institutions, at the time when lawsuits ceased and punishments were clear, still one vacated the mat for the hidden and steadfast to perfect spiritual transformation; the rites of summons and appointment shone into cliffside caves, gifts of jade and silk piled at humble doors—therefore the "Monthly Ordinances" says, "In the last month of spring one hires eminent scholars and treats the worthy with ritual"—does it not mean this?

value.zh: 自典午運開，旁求隱逸，譙元彥之杜絕人事，江思悛之嘯詠林藪，峻其貞白之軌，成其出塵之跡，雖不應其嘉招，亦足激其貪競。
value.en: Since the house of Jin rose, the throne has combed the hills for hidden men: Qiao Xiu shut his gate on the world, Jiang Dun whistled and sang deep in the hills. They raised the standard of unstained integrity and showed how to step outside the scramble for power. They never took the court's gracious offers, yet their example was enough to shame the grasping and the ambitious.
value.literal: From when the Jin fortune opened, seeking far and wide for recluses, as with Qiao Xiuyuan's cutting off human affairs, or Jiang Silun's whistling and chanting in woods and marshes, they made steep the track of chastity and purity, they completed traces beyond the dust; although they did not respond to fine summons, still it was enough to sting greed and rivalry.

value.zh: 今美其高尚之德，綴集於篇。
value.en: Here I gather their stories to honor the height of their character.
value.literal: Now I praise their lofty virtue and string them together in this chapter.

value.zh: 刺史王弘以元熙中臨州，甚欽遲之，後自造焉。
value.en: Wang Hong came to govern and longed to meet him.
value.literal: Inspector Wang Hong in the Yuanxi years came to the province, greatly admired and waited for him, afterward personally visited him.

value.zh: 潛稱疾不見，既而語人云：「我性不狎世，因疾守閑，幸非潔志慕聲，豈敢以王公紆軫為榮邪！
value.en: Qian claimed illness and would not see; afterward said to people, "My nature does not cozy with the world; because of illness I guard quiet—luckily it is not a clean intent admiring fame—how dare I take a prince's bending axle as glory!
value.literal: Qian claimed illness and would not see; afterward said to people, "My nature does not cozy with the world; because of illness I guard quiet—luckily it is not a clean intent admiring fame—how dare I take a prince's bending axle as glory!

value.zh: 夫謬以不賢，此劉公幹所以招謗君子，其罪不細也。」
value.en: To be wrongly deemed unworthy—that is why Liu Gonggan drew slander from gentlemen; the fault is not small."
value.literal: To be wrongly deemed unworthy—that is why Liu Gonggan drew slander from gentlemen; the fault is not small."

value.zh: 弘每令人候之，密知當往廬山，乃遣其故人龐通之等齎酒，先於半道要之。
value.en: Wang Hong sent a friend with wine mid-road to Lu.
value.literal: Hong always ordered men to watch him; secretly knowing he would go to Mount Lu, then sent his old friend Pang Tongzhi and others carrying wine beforehand to waylay him halfway.

value.zh: 潛既遇酒，便引酌野亭，欣然忘進。
value.en: Tao stopped for wine and forgot the journey.
value.literal: When Qian met the wine, he then drew drink in a wild pavilion, gladly forgot to advance.

value.zh: 弘乃出與相見，遂歡宴窮日。
value.en: Wang Hong joined the feast.
value.literal: Hong then came out and met him; then they feasted merrily all day.

value.zh: 潛無履，弘顧左右為之造履。
value.en: Tao had no shoes; Wang ordered sandals made.
value.literal: Qian had no sandals; Hong looked to left and right to have sandals made for him.

value.zh: 左右請履度，潛便於坐申腳令度焉。
value.en: Tao stretched his bare feet to be measured.
value.literal: Attendants asked for foot measure; Qian at the seat stretched out his feet and let them measure.

value.zh: 弘要之還州，問其所乘，答云：「素有腳疾，向乘藍輿，亦足自反。」
value.en: He answered, "Plainly I have foot ailment; lately I ride a blue litter—still enough to return myself."
value.literal: Hong invited him back to the province, asked what he rode; he answered, "Plainly I have foot ailment; lately I ride a blue litter—still enough to return myself."

value.zh: 乃令一門生二兒共轝之至州，而言笑賞適，不覺其有羨于華軒也。
value.en: Students carried his chair; he chatted as if no shame.
value.literal: Then he ordered one student and two sons together to carry him to the province, yet talking and laughing at ease, not letting them feel he envied splendid carriages.

value.zh: 弘後欲見，輒于林澤間候之。
value.en: Wang met him only in the wilds.
value.literal: Hong afterward when wishing to see him, then waited for him among woods and marshes.

value.zh: 至於酒米乏絕，亦時相贍。
value.en: Wang sent grain when the larder ran dry.
value.literal: As for when wine and rice failed, sometimes he also supplied him.

value.zh: 苻洪
value.en: Fu Hong
value.literal: Fu Hong

value.zh: 初，張遇自許昌來降，健納遇後母韓氏為昭儀，每於眾中謂遇曰：「卿，吾子也。」
value.en: At first, when Zhang Yu surrendered from Xuchang, Jian had taken Yu’s stepmother Lady Han as an honored concubine and often said to Yu in public: “You are my son.”
value.literal: At first, when Zhang Yu had surrendered from Xuchang, Jian had taken Yu’s stepmother Lady Han as an honored concubine and often said in public: “You are my son.”

value.zh: 遇慚恨，引關中諸將欲以雍州歸順，乃與健中黃門劉晃謀夜襲健，事覺，遇害。
value.en: Burning with shame, Yu rallied Guanzhong’s commanders to deliver Yong to Jin and conspired with Liu Huang to ambush Jian; the scheme surfaced and Yu died for it.
value.literal: Yu was ashamed and resentful; he drew in the Guanzhong generals intending to hand Yong Province to Jin, and plotted with palace attendant Liu Huang to strike Jian by night; the plot leaked and Yu was killed.

value.zh: 於是孔特起池陽，劉珍、夏侯顯起鄠，喬景起雍，胡陽赤起司竹，呼延毒起霸城，眾數萬人，並遣使詣征西桓溫、中軍殷浩請救。
value.en: Revolt flared: Kong Te at Chiyang, Liu Zhen and Xiahou Xian at Hu, Qiao Jing at Yong, Hu Yangchi at Sizhu, Huyan Du at Bashicheng—each mustered tens of thousands—and all begged Huan Wen and Yin Hao for relief.
value.literal: Thereupon Kong Te rose at Chiyang, Liu Zhen and Xiahou Xian at Hu, Qiao Jing at Yong, Hu Yangchi at Sizhu, Huyan Du at Bashicheng—each with tens of thousands—and all sent envoys to General Who Conquers the West Huan Wen and Central Army commander Yin Hao begging rescue.

value.zh: 馬璘，扶風人也。
value.en: Ma Lin was a native of Fufeng.
value.literal: Ma Lin was a man of Fufeng.

value.zh: 祖正會，右威衛將軍。
value.en: His grandfather Zheng Hui had served as general of the Right Martial Majesty Guard.
value.literal: His grandfather Zheng Hui was Right Martial Majesty Guard general.

value.zh: 父晟，右司禦率府兵曹參軍。
value.en: His father Sheng was registrar of military affairs in the Right Imperial Guard Training Corps.
value.literal: His father Sheng was military affairs registrar of the Right Imperial Guard Training Bureau.

value.zh: 璘少孤，落拓不事生業。
value.en: Lin lost his parents early and lived unconstrained, without taking up any regular occupation.
value.literal: Lin was orphaned young, unrestrained and not pursuing any livelihood.

value.zh: 年二十余，讀《馬援傳》至「大丈夫當死於邊野，以馬革裹屍而歸」，慨然嘆曰：「豈使吾祖勛業墜於地乎！」
value.en: In his early twenties he read the biography of Ma Yuan as far as the line that a great man ought to die on the frontier, his body wrapped in horsehide for the journey home, and exclaimed with feeling, "Am I to let my forebears' achievements come to nothing?"
value.literal: When he was a little over twenty, reading the biography of Ma Yuan to the passage "A great man ought to die on the frontier wilds, his corpse wrapped in horsehide for the return home," he sighed in emotion and said, "Shall I let my ancestors' achievements fall to the ground?"

value.zh: 開元末，杖劍從戎，自效於安西。
value.en: At the close of the Kaiyuan reign he took up the sword and entered military service, volunteering in the Anxi Protectorate.
value.literal: At the end of the Kaiyuan era he took sword in hand to join the army and offered himself in Anxi.

value.zh: 以前後奇功，累遷至左金吾衛將軍同正。
value.en: Through a series of remarkable feats he rose step by step to acting general of the Left Golden Crow Guard.
value.literal: Because of repeated extraordinary achievements he was promoted in succession to acting Left Golden Crow Guard general.

value.zh: 茂元，幼有勇略，從父征伐知名。
value.en: Maoyuan showed courage and tactical skill from youth and won fame campaigning with his father.
value.literal: Maoyuan in his youth had courage and stratagem; following his father in campaigns he became renowned.

value.zh: 元和中，為右神策將軍。
value.en: During the Yuanhe reign he served as a general of the Right Shence Army.
value.literal: In the Yuanhe era he was Right Shence Army general.

value.zh: 太和中，檢校工部尚書、廣州刺史、嶺南節度使。
value.en: In the Taihe era he became acting Minister of Works, prefect of Guangzhou, and military governor of Lingnan.
value.literal: In the Taihe era he was acting Minister of Works, prefect of Guangzhou, and Lingnan military governor.

value.zh: 在安南招懷蠻落，頗立政能。
value.en: In Annan he won over the tribal peoples and governed with notable effectiveness.
value.literal: In Annan he recruited and reassured the tribal settlements and established considerable administrative ability.

value.zh: 南中多異貨，茂元積聚家財鉅萬計。
value.en: The south abounded in exotic goods, and Maoyuan accumulated a family fortune of many millions.
value.literal: The south had many exotic goods; Maoyuan amassed family wealth to the number of tens of millions.

value.zh: 李訓之敗，中官利其財，掎摭其事，言茂元因王涯、鄭註見用。
value.en: After Li Xun's downfall the eunuchs coveted his wealth and denounced him, claiming he had risen through the patronage of Wang Ya and Zheng Zhu.
value.literal: When Li Xun's plot failed, the inner court eunuchs coveted his wealth and seized on his affairs, saying Maoyuan had been employed through Wang Ya and Zheng Zhu.

value.zh: 茂元懼，罄家財以賂兩軍，以是授忠武軍節度、陳許觀察使。
value.en: Fearing ruin, Maoyuan spent his entire fortune bribing the two armies and was transferred to military governor of the Zhongwu Army and observation commissioner of Chen and Xu.
value.literal: Maoyuan feared this and exhausted his family wealth to bribe the two armies; because of this he was appointed Zhongwu Army military governor and Chenxu observation commissioner.

value.zh: 會昌中，為河陽節度使。
value.en: During the Huichang reign he served as military governor of Hanyang.
value.literal: In the Huichang era he was Hanyang military governor.

value.zh: 是時河北諸軍討劉稹，茂元亦以本軍屯天井，賊未平而卒。
value.en: When the Hebei armies campaigned against Liu Zhen, Maoyuan encamped at Tianjing with his own troops but died before the rebellion was crushed.
value.literal: At that time the Hebei armies attacked Liu Zhen; Maoyuan also encamped his own army at Tianjing, and before the rebels were pacified he died.

value.zh: 梁書卷第四十 列傳第三十四
value.en: Book of Liang, Volume 40, Biography 34
value.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 40, Biography 34

value.zh: 顯有三子：莠，荏，臻。
value.en: Xian had three sons—You, Ren, and Zhen.
value.literal: Xian had three sons: You, Ren, and Zhen.

value.zh: 臻早著名。
value.en: Zhen was famed from early on.
value.literal: Zhen early won renown.

value.zh: 梁書卷第四十一 列傳第三十五
value.en: Book of Liang, Volume 41, Biography 35
value.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 41, Biography 35

value.zh: 孺幼聰敏，七歲能屬文。
value.en: Ru was bright and sharp as a boy; at seven he could already write.
value.literal: Ru was clever and keen from childhood; at seven he could compose prose.

value.zh: 年十四，居父喪，毀瘠骨立，宗黨咸異之。
value.en: At fourteen he mourned his father until he was skin and bone; kinsmen and neighbors were astonished.
value.literal: At fourteen, while mourning his father, he wasted away until only bone remained, and all his kin marveled at him.

value.zh: 服闋，叔父瑱爲義興郡，攜以之官，常置坐側，謂賓客曰：「此兒吾家之明珠也。」
value.en: When mourning ended his uncle Zhen governed Yixing and brought him along, keeping him always at his side, and said to guests, "This child is the pearl of our clan."
value.literal: When mourning ended his uncle Zhen was interior minister of Yixing and took him to his post, always seating him at his side, and told guests: "This boy is the pearl of our house."

value.zh: 旣長，美風采，性通和，雖家人不見其喜慍。
value.en: Grown handsome in bearing and even-tempered, even his own household never caught him in joy or anger.
value.literal: When grown he was handsome in bearing, open and harmonious by nature, and even at home none saw him show pleasure or anger.

value.zh: 本州召迎主簿。
value.en: His home province called him to be registrar.
value.literal: The province summoned him to serve as registrar.

value.zh: 到沆 丘遲 劉苞 袁峻 庾於陵 弟肩吾 劉昭 何遜 鍾嶸 周興嗣 吳均
value.en: Dao Hang · Qiu Chi · Liu Bao · Yuan Jun · Yu Yuling · Jianwu (brother) · Liu Zhao · He Xun · Zhong Rong · Zhou Xingsi · Wu Jun
value.literal: Dao Hang, Qiu Chi, Liu Bao, Yuan Jun, Yu Yuling, younger brother Jianwu, Liu Zhao, He Xun, Zhong Rong, Zhou Xingsi, Wu Jun

value.zh: 氣之動物，物之感人，故搖盪性情，形諸舞詠。
value.en: Qi moves things; things move people—so feeling stirs and finds form in dance and song.
value.literal: When qi stirs things, things move people; thus feelings sway and take shape in dance and song.

value.zh: 欲以照燭三才，輝麗萬有，靈祇待之以致饗，幽微藉之以昭告。
value.en: It lights the three powers and adorns the myriad; spirits wait on it for sacrifice, the hidden use it to declare.
value.literal: It means to illuminate the three realms and shed glory on the myriad beings; spirits await it for offerings, and the hidden and subtle rely on it for proclamation.

value.zh: 動天地，感鬼神，莫近於詩。
value.en: To move Heaven and Earth and touch gods and ghosts, nothing nears poetry.
value.literal: Moving Heaven and Earth, touching spirits and ghosts—nothing comes nearer than poetry.

value.zh: 昔《南風》之辭，《卿雲》之頌，厥義夐矣。
value.en: Of old Southern Winds and Cloud-Coach—their meaning was already vast.
value.literal: Of old the words of the *Southern Winds* and the hymn *Cloud-Coach*—their meaning was already far-reaching.

value.zh: 《夏歌》曰「郁陶乎予心」，楚謠云「名余曰正則」，雖詩體未全，然略是五言之濫觴也。
value.en: Xia Songs have "deeply troubled in heart"; Chu songs name "Zhengze"—verse form was incomplete, yet these were the springs of five-character poetry.
value.literal: The *Xia Songs* say "I am deeply troubled in heart"; a Chu song says "They named me Zhengze"—though the poetic form was not yet complete, they were roughly the source of five-character verse.

value.zh: 逮漢李陵，始著五言之目。
value.en: By Han, Li Ling first established five-character verse as a category.
value.literal: Down to Han's Li Ling, the category of five-character verse was first set forth.

value.zh: 古詩眇邈，人代難詳，推其文體，固是炎漢之制，非衰周之倡也。
value.en: Ancient poems are distant and ages obscure; by form they belong to Han, not late Zhou.
value.literal: Ancient poems are remote and ages hard to trace; judging their form, they are truly products of blazing Han, not songs of declining Zhou.

value.zh: 自王、揚、枚、馬之徒，辭賦競爽，而吟詠靡聞。
value.en: From Wang Bao, Yang Xiong, Mei Cheng, and Sima Xiangru on, fu competed in brilliance while lyric verse was rarely heard.
value.literal: From Wang, Yang, Mei, and Ma onward, rhapsodies vied in brilliance, yet lyric singing was scarcely heard.

value.zh: 從李都尉訖班婕妤，將百年間，有婦人焉，一人而已。
value.en: From Li Ling to Lady Ban, nearly a century held one woman poet—and only one.
value.literal: From Commandant Li to Lady Ban, in nearly a hundred years there was a woman—and only one.

value.zh: 詩人之風，頓已缺喪。
value.en: The poets' wind had suddenly died away.
value.literal: The poets' tradition had suddenly perished.

value.zh: 東京二百載中，唯有班固《詠史》，質木無文致。
value.en: Eastern Han's two centuries held only Ban Gu's Ode on History—plain and without literary grace.
value.literal: In the two hundred years of Eastern Han there was only Ban Gu's *Ode on History*—plain wood without literary grace.

value.zh: 降及建安，曹公父子，篤好斯文；
value.en: By Jian'an, the Cao lord and his sons deeply loved letters;
value.literal: Down to the Jian'an period, Lord Cao and his sons deeply loved this craft;

value.zh: 平原兄弟，鬱爲文棟；
value.en: the Pingyuan brothers rose as literary pillars;
value.literal: the brothers of Pingyuan flourished as literary pillars;

value.zh: 劉楨、王粲，爲其羽冀。
value.en: Liu Zhen and Wang Can were their wings.
value.literal: Liu Zhen and Wang Can were their wings.

value.zh: 次有攀龍託鳳，自致於屬車者，蓋將百計。
value.en: Next came nearly a hundred who clung to dragons and phoenixes and joined the train.
value.literal: Next came those who, clinging to dragons and nesting phoenixes, attached themselves to the rear train—nearly a hundred in number.

value.zh: 彬彬之盛，大備於時矣！
value.en: Such abundant flowering was complete in that age!
value.literal: Such abundant flourishing was fully prepared in that age!

value.zh: 爾後陵遲衰微，訖於有晉。
value.en: Afterward it declined to Jin.
value.literal: Afterward it declined and weakened, down to Jin.

value.zh: 太康中，三張二陸，兩潘一左，勃爾復興，踵武前王，風流未沫，亦文章之中興也。
value.en: Taikang saw the three Zhangs, two Lus, two Pans, and Zuo Zuo revive the art—wind not yet spent, a literary revival.
value.literal: In the Taikang era the three Zhangs, two Lus, two Pans, and one Zuo suddenly flourished again, following the martial ways of former kings; the breeze had not yet dried—this too was a literary revival.

value.zh: 永嘉時，貴黃、老，尚虛談，于時篇什，理過其辭，淡乎寡味。
value.en: Yongjia honored Huang-Lao and pure talk; verse reasoned past its words—thin and flavorless.
value.literal: In the Yongjia era Yellow Lao and empty talk were honored; poems of the time reasoned beyond their words and were thin and tasteless.

value.zh: 爰及江表，微波尚傳，孫綽、許詢、桓、庾諸公，皆平典似《道德論》，建安之風盡矣。
value.en: South of the river slight ripples remained; Sun Chuo, Xu Xun, Huan, and Yu wrote level pieces like the Dao De Lun—Jian'an's wind was gone.
value.literal: Reaching the lands south of the Yangtze, slight ripples still passed on; Sun Chuo, Xu Xun, Huan, Yu, and the gentlemen were all level and canonical like the *Dao De Lun*—Jian'an's wind was wholly gone.

value.zh: 先是郭景純用俊上之才，創變其體；
value.en: Earlier Guo Jingchun, with lofty talent, changed the form;
value.literal: Earlier Guo Pu, with lofty talent, innovated and changed the form;

value.zh: 劉越石仗清剛之氣，贊成厥美。
value.en: Liu Yueshi, with pure firm spirit, helped perfect that beauty.
value.literal: Liu Kun, relying on pure firmness, helped perfect that beauty.

value.zh: 然彼衆我寡，未能動俗。
value.en: Yet the many outweighed the few and could not shift custom.
value.literal: Yet they were many against few and could not move custom.

value.zh: 逮義熙中，謝益壽斐然繼作；
value.en: By Yixi Xie Lingyun flourished and continued writing;
value.literal: By the Yixi era Xie Lingyun flourished and continued the work;

value.zh: 元嘉初，有謝靈運，才高辭盛，富豔難蹤，固已含跨劉、郭，陵轢潘、左。
value.en: Early Yuanjia brought Xie Lingyun—great talent, rich diction, splendor hard to follow; he spanned Liu and Guo and towered over Pan and Zuo.
value.literal: At the beginning of Yuanjia there was Xie Lingyun—talent high, diction rich, splendor hard to track; he already spanned Liu and Guo and towered over Pan and Zuo.

value.zh: 故知陳思爲建安之傑，公幹、仲宣爲輔；
value.en: Thus Prince Si was Jian'an's crown, Gonggan and Zhongxuan his aides;
value.literal: Thus we know Prince Si was Jian'an's paragon, with Gonggan and Zhongxuan as aides;

value.zh: 陸機爲太康之英，安仁、景陽爲輔；
value.en: Lu Ji was Taikang's hero, Anren and Jingyang his aides;
value.literal: Lu Ji was Taikang's hero, with Anren and Jingyang as aides;

value.zh: 謝客爲元嘉之雄，顏延年爲輔：此皆五言之冠冕，文辭之命世。
value.en: Guest Xie was Yuanjia's champion, Yan Yannian his aide—these crown five-character verse and master an age of letters.
value.literal: Guest Xie was Yuanjia's champion, with Yan Yannian as aide: these are the crowns of five-character verse, fated masters of letters.

value.zh: 興宗一
value.en: Xingzong, Part One
value.literal: Xingzong, Part One

value.zh: 十一年夏六月己卯，聖宗崩，即皇帝位於柩前。
value.en: In the eleventh year, on jimao day of the sixth summer month Shengzong died, and [the heir] immediately took the throne before the coffin.
value.literal: In the eleventh year, summer, sixth month, on jimao day, Shengzong died; immediately took the imperial throne before the coffin.

value.zh: 壬午，尊母元妃蕭氏為皇太后。
value.en: On renwu day the new Emperor honored his mother, Lady Xiao, as Empress Dowager.
value.literal: On renwu day, honored mother Lady Xiao as Empress Dowager.

value.zh: 甲申，遣使告哀於宋及夏、高麗。
value.en: On jiashen day envoys were dispatched to announce the mourning to Song, Xia, and Goryeo.
value.literal: On jiashen day, dispatched envoys to announce the mourning to Song, Xia, and Goryeo.

value.zh: 是年，禦宣政殿放進士劉貞等五十七人。
value.en: That year jinshi examinations were held at Xuanzheng Hall and fifty-seven candidates including Liu Zhen passed.
value.literal: That year, held jinshi examination at Xuanzheng Hall and released fifty-seven including Liu Zhen.

value.zh: 辛卯，大赦，改元景福。
value.en: On xinmao day a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed to Jingfu.
value.literal: On xinmao day, general amnesty; changed era name to Jingfu.

value.zh: 乙未，奉大行皇帝梓宮，殯於永安山太平殿。
value.en: On yiwei day the late Emperor's coffin was escorted and encoffined at Taiping Hall on Yong'an Mountain.
value.literal: On yiwei day, escorted the late Emperor's coffin and encoffined it at Taiping Hall on Yong'an Mountain.

value.zh: 辛丑，皇太后賜駙馬蕭鉏不裏、蕭匹敵死，圍場都太師女直著骨裏、右祗候郎君詳穩蕭延留等七人皆棄市，籍其家，遷齊天皇后於上京。
value.en: On xinchou day the Empress Dowager ordered imperial son-in-law Xiao Cubu and Xiao Pide to death; Hunt-grounds grand preceptor Jurchen Zhuguli, Right Assistant Attendant langjun xiangwen Xiao Yanliu, and seven others were all executed in the marketplace; their households were confiscated; and Empress Qi Tian was moved to the Upper Capital.
value.literal: On xinchou day, the Empress Dowager ordered imperial son-in-law Xiao Cubu to death and Xiao Pide to death; Hunt-grounds grand preceptor Jurchen Zhuguli, Right Assistant Attendant langjun xiangwen Xiao Yanliu, and seven others were all executed in the marketplace; their households were confiscated; Empress Qi Tian was moved to the Upper Capital.

value.zh: 秋七月丙午朔，皇太后率皇族大臨於太平殿。
value.en: On the bingwu new moon of the seventh autumn month the Empress Dowager led the imperial clan in great mourning at Taiping Hall.
value.literal: In autumn, seventh month, on the bingwu new moon, the Empress Dowager led the imperial clan in great mourning at Taiping Hall.

value.zh: 高麗遣使吊慰。
value.en: Goryeo dispatched envoys to express condolences.
value.literal: Goryeo dispatched envoys to express condolences.

value.zh: 上召晉王蕭普古等飲博，夜分乃罷。
value.en: The Emperor summoned Prince of Jin Xiao Pugu and others to drink and gamble; only at midnight did they stop.
value.literal: The Emperor summoned Prince of Jin Xiao Pugu and others to drink and gamble; only at midnight did they stop.

value.zh: 丁未，擊鞠。
value.en: On dingwei day the court played cuju.
value.literal: On dingwei day, played cuju.

value.zh: 戊申，以耶律韓八為左夷離畢，特末裏為左祗候郎君詳穩，橫帳郎君樂古權右祗候郎君祥穩。
value.en: On wushen day Yelü Hanba was appointed Left yilibi; Temuli was made Left Assistant Attendant langjun xiangwen; and Cross-Tent langjun Yegu acting Right Assistant Attendant langjun xiangwen.
value.literal: On wushen day, made Yelü Hanba Left yilibi, Temuli Left Assistant Attendant langjun xiangwen, and Cross-Tent langjun Yegu acting Right Assistant Attendant langjun xiangwen.

value.zh: 己酉，以耶律鄭留為於厥迪烈都詳穩，高八為右皮室詳穩。
value.en: On jiyou day Yelü Zhengliu was appointed Ugu diledu xiangwen and Gao Ba Right Pishi xiangwen.
value.literal: On jiyou day, made Yelü Zhengliu Ugu diledu xiangwen and Gao Ba Right Pishi xiangwen.

value.zh: 庚戌，賑薊州民饑。
value.en: On gengxu day relief was provided for hungry people in Jizhou.
value.literal: On gengxu day, provided relief for hungry people in Jizhou.

value.zh: 癸丑，詔寫大行皇帝御容。
value.en: On guichou day an edict ordered the late Emperor's portrait painted.
value.literal: On guichou day, edict ordered painting of the late Emperor's portrait.

value.zh: 甲寅，錄囚。
value.en: On jiayin day prisoners were reviewed.
value.literal: On jiayin day, reviewed prisoners.

value.zh: 以觀察姚居信為上將軍。
value.en: Observation commissioner Yao Juxin was appointed upper general.
value.literal: Made observation commissioner Yao Juxin upper general.

value.zh: 建慶州於慶陵之南，徙民實之，充奉陵邑。
value.en: Qingzhou was built south of Qing Mausoleum; people were moved to fill it, serving as a mausoleum-attendant settlement.
value.literal: Built Qingzhou south of Qing Mausoleum, moved people to fill it, serving as mausoleum-attendant settlement.

value.zh: 乙卯，以比歲豐稔，罷給東京統軍司糧。
value.en: On yimao day, because grain harvests had been abundant in recent years, grain supplies to the Eastern Capital military governor's office were discontinued.
value.literal: On yimao day, because grain harvest had been abundant in recent years, ceased supplying grain to the Eastern Capital military governor's office.

value.zh: 丁巳，上謁大行皇帝御容，哀慟久之。
value.en: On dingsi day the Emperor visited the late Emperor's portrait and mourned deeply for a long time.
value.literal: On dingsi day, the Emperor visited the late Emperor's portrait and mourned deeply for a long time.

value.zh: 因詔寫北府宰相蕭孝先、南府宰相蕭孝穆像於御容殿。
value.en: Thereupon an edict ordered portraits of Northern Chancellor Xiao Xiaoxian and Southern Chancellor Xiao Xiaomu painted in the Imperial Portrait Hall.
value.literal: Thereupon edict ordered painting portraits of Northern Chancellor Xiao Xiaoxian and Southern Chancellor Xiao Xiaomu in the Imperial Portrait Hall.

value.zh: 以蕭阿姑軫為東京留守。
value.en: Xiao Aguzhen was appointed Eastern Capital regent.
value.literal: Made Xiao Aguzhen Eastern Capital regent.

value.zh: 丁卯，謁太平殿，焚先帝所禦弓矢。
value.en: On dingmao day the court visited Taiping Hall and burned the late Emperor's bow and arrows.
value.literal: On dingmao day, visited Taiping Hall and burned the late Emperor's bow and arrows.

value.zh: 幸晉王普古第視疾。
value.en: The court visited Prince of Jin Pugu's residence to inquire after his illness.
value.literal: Visited Prince of Jin Pugu's residence to inquire after his illness.

value.zh: 辛未，錄囚。
value.en: On xinwei day prisoners were reviewed.
value.literal: On xinwei day, reviewed prisoners.

value.zh: 壬申，上謁神主帳，時奧隈蕭氏始入宮，亦命拜之。
value.en: On renshen day the Emperor visited the tent containing the spirit tablets; at that time aowei Lady Xiao had just entered the palace, and she too was ordered to bow before them.
value.literal: On renshen day, the Emperor visited the spirit-tablet tent; at that time aowei Lady Xiao had just entered the palace, and she too was ordered to bow before the tablets.

value.zh: 八月壬午，遷大行皇帝梓宮於菆塗殿。
value.en: In the eighth month, on renwu day, the late Emperor's coffin was moved to Zutu Hall.
value.literal: In the eighth month, on renwu day, moved the late Emperor's coffin to Zutu Hall.

value.zh: 九月戊申，躬視慶陵。
value.en: In the ninth month, on wushen day, the Emperor personally inspected Qing Mausoleum.
value.literal: In the ninth month, on wushen day, personally inspected Qing Mausoleum.

value.zh: 庚戌，問安於皇太后。
value.en: On gengxu day the Emperor paid respects to the Empress Dowager.
value.literal: On gengxu day, paid respects to the Empress Dowager.

value.zh: 辛亥，宋遣王隨、曹儀致祭，王鬷、許懷信、梅詢、張綸來慰兩宮，範諷、孫繼業賀即位，孔道輔、魏昭文賀皇太吊後冊禮。
value.en: On xinhai day Song sent Wang Sui and Cao Yi to perform sacrifices; Wang Ji, Xu Huaixin, Mei Xun, and Zhang Lun came to console the two palaces; Fan Feng and Sun Jiye congratulated on the accession; and Kong Daofu and Wei Zhaowen congratulated on the Empress Dowager's post-mourning investiture rites.
value.literal: On xinhai day, Song sent Wang Sui and Cao Yi to perform sacrifices; Wang Ji, Xu Huaixin, Mei Xun, and Zhang Lun came to console the two palaces; Fan Feng and Sun Jiye congratulated on the accession; Kong Daofu and Wei Zhaowen congratulated on the Empress Dowager's post-mourning investiture rites.

value.zh: 戊午，焚弧矢、鞍勒於菆塗殿。
value.en: On wuwu day bows, arrows, saddle, and bridle were burned at Zutu Hall.
value.literal: On wuwu day, burned bows, arrows, saddle, and bridle at Zutu Hall.

value.zh: 庚申，夏國遣使來慰。
value.en: On gengshen day Xia State sent envoys with condolences.
value.literal: On gengshen day, Xia State sent envoys with condolences.

value.zh: 庚午，以宋使吊祭，喪服臨菆塗殿。
value.en: On gengwu day, because Song envoys came to mourn and sacrifice, the Emperor wore mourning dress and attended at Zutu Hall.
value.literal: On gengwu day, because Song envoys came to mourn and sacrifice, wore mourning dress and attended at Zutu Hall.

value.zh: 甲戌，遣御史中丞耶律翥、司農卿張確、詳穩耶律勵、四方館使高維翰謝宋吊慰。
value.en: On jiaxu day Censorate Vice Director Yelü Xu, Minister of Agriculture Zhang Que, xiangwen Yelü Li, and Four Directions Bureau envoy Gao Weihan were dispatched to thank Song for condolences.
value.literal: On jiaxu day, dispatched Censorate Vice Director Yelü Xu, Minister of Agriculture Zhang Que, xiangwen Yelü Li, and Four Directions Bureau envoy Gao Weihan to thank Song for condolences.

value.zh: 冬十月戊寅，宰臣呂德懋薨。
value.en: On wuyin day of the tenth winter month chief minister Lü Demao died.
value.literal: In winter, tenth month, on wuyin day, chief minister Lü Demao died.

value.zh: 癸未，殺鉏不裏黨彌勒奴、觀音奴等。
value.en: On guiwei day Cubu faction members Mile Nu, Guanyin Nu, and others were executed.
value.literal: On guiwei day, killed Cubu faction members Mile Nu, Guanyin Nu, and others.

value.zh: 丙戌，遣工部尚書高德順、崇祿卿李可封致先帝遺物於宋；
value.en: On bingxu day Minister of Works Gao Deshun and Chamberlain for Imperial Insignia Li Kefeng were dispatched to present the late Emperor's bequests to Song;
value.literal: On bingxu day, dispatched Minister of Works Gao Deshun and Chamberlain for Imperial Insignia Li Kefeng to present the late Emperor's bequests to Song;

value.zh: 以右領軍衛上將軍耶律遜、少府監馬憚充皇太后謝宋使；
value.en: Right Imperial Guard upper general Yelü Xun and Palace Manufactories supervisor Ma Dan were appointed envoys to thank Song on behalf of the Empress Dowager;
value.literal: made Right Imperial Guard upper general Yelü Xun and Palace Manufactories supervisor Ma Dan envoys to thank Song on behalf of the Empress Dowager;

value.zh: 右監門衛上將軍耶律元載、引進使魏永充皇帝謝宋使。
value.en: Right Palace Gate Guard upper general Yelü Yuanzai and presenting envoy Wei Yong served as the Emperor's envoys to thank Song.
value.literal: Right Palace Gate Guard upper general Yelü Yuanzai and presenting envoy Wei Yong served as the Emperor's envoys to thank Song.

value.zh: 丁酉，夏國遣使來賻。
value.en: On dingyou day Xia State sent envoys with funeral gifts.
value.literal: On dingyou day, Xia State sent envoys with funeral gifts.

value.zh: 戊戌，以蕭革、趙為果、耶律郁、馬保業充來歲賀宋正旦使副。
value.en: On wuxu day Xiao Ge, Zhao Weiguo, Yelü Yu, and Ma Baoye were appointed chief and deputy envoys to congratulate Song on New Year's Day of the coming year.
value.literal: On wuxu day, appointed Xiao Ge, Zhao Weiguo, Yelü Yu, and Ma Baoye chief and deputy envoys to congratulate Song on New Year's Day of the coming year.

value.zh: 閏月辛亥，謁菆塗殿，閱玄宮器。
value.en: In the intercalary month, on xinhai day, the court visited Zutu Hall and inspected inner-chamber vessels.
value.literal: In the intercalary month, on xinhai day, visited Zutu Hall and inspected inner-chamber vessels.

value.zh: 有司請以生辰為永壽節，皇太后生辰為應聖節，從之。
value.en: The relevant offices requested making the Emperor's birthday the Eternal Longevity Festival and the Empress Dowager's birthday the Responding Sage Festival; approval was granted.
value.literal: The relevant offices requested making the birthday the Eternal Longevity Festival and the Empress Dowager's birthday the Responding Sage Festival; approved.

value.zh: 辛酉，閱新造鎧甲。
value.en: On xinyou day newly made armor was inspected.
value.literal: On xinyou day, inspected newly made armor.

value.zh: 丁卯，振黃龍府饑民。
value.en: On dingmao day hungry people in Huanglong Prefecture were relieved.
value.literal: On dingmao day, relieved hungry people in Huanglong Prefecture.

value.zh: 十一月壬辰，上率百僚奠於菆塗殿。
value.en: On renchen day of the eleventh month the Emperor led all officials in offerings at Zutu Hall.
value.literal: In the eleventh month, on renchen day, the Emperor led all officials in offerings at Zutu Hall.

value.zh: 出大行皇帝服御、玩好焚之。
value.en: The late Emperor's clothing, accoutrements, and treasured articles were brought out and burned.
value.literal: Brought out the late Emperor's clothing, accoutrements, and treasured articles and burned them.

value.zh: 縱五坊鷹鶻。
value.en: The five-compound hawks and falcons were released.
value.literal: Released the five-compound hawks and falcons.

value.zh: 甲午，葬文武大孝宣皇帝於慶陵。
value.en: On jiawu day the Cultured and Martial Great Filial Xuan Emperor was buried at Qing Mausoleum.
value.literal: On jiawu day, buried the Cultured and Martial Great Filial Xuan Emperor at Qing Mausoleum.

value.zh: 乙未，祭天地。
value.en: On yiwei day sacrifices were offered to Heaven and Earth.
value.literal: On yiwei day, sacrificed to Heaven and Earth.

value.zh: 問安皇太后。
value.en: The Emperor paid respects to the Empress Dowager.
value.literal: Paid respects to the Empress Dowager.

value.zh: 丙申，謁慶陵，以遺物賜群臣，名其山曰慶雲，殿曰望仙。
value.en: On bingshen day the court visited Qing Mausoleum, bestowed bequest articles on ministers, named the mountain Qingyun, and named the hall Wangxian.
value.literal: On bingshen day, visited Qing Mausoleum, bestowed bequest articles on ministers, named the mountain Qingyun, and the hall Wangxian.

value.zh: 十二月癸丑，至自慶陵。
value.en: On guichou day of the twelfth month the court returned from Qing Mausoleum.
value.literal: In the twelfth month, on guichou day, returned from Qing Mausoleum.

value.zh: 皇太后聽政，帝不親庶務，群臣表請，不從。
value.en: The Empress Dowager held court; the Emperor did not personally handle routine affairs; ministers memorialized requesting that he do so, but he did not agree.
value.literal: The Empress Dowager held court; the Emperor did not personally handle routine affairs; ministers memorialized requesting [him to], but he did not agree.

value.zh: 是歲，以興平公主下嫁夏國王李德昭子元昊，以元昊為夏國公、駙馬都尉。
value.en: That year Princess Xingping was married to Li Dezhao's son Yuanhao of Xia State; Yuanhao was made Duke of Xia State and Commandant of Imperial Son-in-law.
value.literal: That year, Princess Xingping was married to Li Dezhao's son Yuanhao of Xia State; Yuanhao was made Duke of Xia State and Commandant of Imperial Son-in-law.

value.zh: 燕兵之襲大寧也，守將都指揮卜萬與都督劉真、陳亨帥兵扼松亭關。
value.en: During the Yan assault on Daling, garrison commander Bu Wan and commissioners Liu Zhen and Chen Heng held Songting Pass with their troops.
value.literal: When Yan troops raided Daling, defending commander Bu Wan and Commissioners Liu Zhen and Chen Heng led troops to block Songting Pass.

value.zh: 亨欲降燕，畏萬，不敢發。
value.en: Chen Heng wanted to defect to the Prince of Yan but feared Bu Wan and held back.
value.literal: Heng wished to surrender to Yan but feared Wan and did not dare act.

value.zh: 燕行反間，貽萬書，盛稱萬；
value.en: The Yan side ran a counter-intelligence scheme, sending Bu Wan a letter that lavishly praised him;
value.literal: Yan carried out a counter-intelligence plot, sending Wan a letter lavishly praising Wan;

value.zh: 極詆亨。
value.en: while viciously denouncing Chen Heng.
value.literal: and bitterly slandering Heng.

value.zh: 厚賞所獲大寧卒，緘書衣中，俾密與萬。
value.en: They richly rewarded captured soldiers from Daling, hid the letter in their clothes, and had them deliver it secretly to Bu Wan.
value.literal: They richly rewarded captured Daling soldiers, sealed the letter in their clothing, and had them secretly give it to Wan.

value.zh: 故使同獲卒見之，亦縱去而不與賞。
value.en: They made sure other captives saw this favor, then released those men without paying them.
value.literal: They deliberately let fellow-captured soldiers see this, and also released them without giving reward.

value.zh: 不得賞者發其事。
value.en: The men who went unrewarded reported what had happened.
value.literal: Those who received no reward exposed the affair.

value.zh: 真、亨搜卒衣，得書。
value.en: Liu Zhen and Chen Heng searched the men's clothing and found the letter.
value.literal: Zhen and Heng searched the soldiers' clothes and obtained the letter.

value.zh: 遂執萬下獄死，籍其家。
value.en: Bu Wan was arrested, died in prison, and his property was confiscated.
value.literal: Thereupon they seized Wan, imprisoned him until he died, and confiscated his household.

value.zh: 萬忠勇而死於間，論者惜之。
value.en: Bu Wan was loyal and courageous yet died by treachery; observers mourned the waste of it.
value.literal: Wan was loyal and brave yet died through intrigue; commentators regretted it.

value.zh: 及大寧陷，指揮使朱鑒力戰，不屈死。
value.en: When Daling fell, Commander Zhu Jian fought to the end and died rather than submit.
value.literal: When Daling fell, Commander Zhu Jian fought fiercely, refused submission, and died.

value.literal: ○ Song Cheng, Xue Lu

value.zh: 蔣貴
value.en: Jiang Gui
value.literal: Jiang Gui

value.zh: （孫琬）
value.en: (Sun Wan)
value.literal: (Sun Wan)

value.zh: 任禮趙安趙輔劉聚宋晟，字景陽，定遠人。
value.en: Ren Li, Zhao An, Zhao Fu, and Liu Ju. Song Cheng, styled Jingyang, was a native of Dingyuan.
value.literal: Ren Li, Zhao An, Zhao Fu, Liu Ju. Song Cheng, styled Jingyang, was a man of Dingyuan.

value.zh: 父朝用，兄國興，並從渡江，皆積功至元帥。
value.en: His father Chaoyong and elder brother Guoxing both followed in the crossing of the Yangtze and, through accumulated merit, rose to the rank of commander.
value.literal: His father Chaoyong and elder brother Guoxing both followed in crossing the Yangtze, both accumulating merit until reaching commander.

value.zh: 攻集慶，國興戰歿，晟嗣其職。
value.en: During the attack on Jiqing, Guoxing was killed in battle, and Cheng succeeded to his command.
value.literal: Attacking Jiqing, Guoxing died in battle; Cheng succeeded to his post.

value.zh: 既而朝用請老，晟方從鄧愈克徽州，召還，襲父官。
value.en: When Chaoyong later requested retirement, Cheng was with Deng Yu capturing Huizhou. Recalled from the campaign, he inherited his father's post.
value.literal: Thereafter Chaoyong requested retirement; Cheng was just following Deng Yu in capturing Huizhou—recalled, he inherited his father's office.

value.zh: 累進都指揮同知，歷鎮江西、大同、陜西。
value.en: He was promoted step by step to regional military commissioner of the third rank and successively served as regional commander in Jiangxi, Datong, and Shaanxi.
value.literal: Repeatedly promoted to regional military commissioner of the third rank, successively commanding at Jiangxi, Datong, and Shaanxi.

value.zh: 洪武十二年坐法降涼州衛指揮使。
value.en: In the twelfth year of Hongwu he was demoted for an offense to garrison commander of Liangzhou Guard.
value.literal: In the twelfth year of Hongwu, through violation of law he was demoted to garrison commander of Liangzhou Guard.

value.zh: 十七年五月討西番叛酋，至亦集乃路，擒元海道千戶也先帖木兒、國公吳把都剌赤等，俘獲萬八千人，送酋長京師，簡其精銳千人補卒伍，余悉放遣。
value.en: In the fifth month of the seventeenth year he marched against rebel chieftains of the western tribes. Reaching Yijina'i Road, he captured the Yuan maritime-route chiliarch Esentemür, the state duke Wu Badur chi, and others—altogether eighteen thousand captives. He sent the chieftains to the capital, drafted one thousand of their best troops into the ranks, and released the remainder.
value.literal: In the fifth month of the seventeenth year he campaigned against the rebellious chieftains of the western barbarians; reaching Yijina'i Road, he captured the Yuan maritime-route chiliarch Esentemür, the state duke Wu Badur chi, and others, taking captive eighteen thousand persons; he sent the chieftains to the capital, selected one thousand elite men to fill the ranks, and released the rest entirely.

value.zh: 召還，復為都指揮，進右軍都督僉事，仍鎮涼州。
value.en: Recalled to court, he was restored as regional commander, promoted to assistant regional commander of the Rear Army, and continued to hold command at Liangzhou.
value.literal: Recalled, he again became regional commander, advanced to assistant regional commander of the Rear Army, and still commanded at Liangzhou.

value.zh: 二十四年充總兵官，與都督劉真討哈梅裏。
value.en: In the twenty-fourth year he served as overall commander and, with Commissioner-in-Chief Liu Zhen, campaigned against Hami.
value.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he served as overall commander, together with Commissioner-in-Chief Liu Zhen campaigning against Hami.

value.zh: 其地去肅州千餘里。
value.en: Hami lay more than a thousand li from Suzhou.
value.literal: That place was more than a thousand li from Suzhou.

value.zh: 晟令軍中多具糧糗，倍道疾馳，乘夜至城下。
value.en: Cheng had the army carry abundant dry rations and forced a rapid march, reaching the city walls under cover of night.
value.literal: Cheng ordered the army to prepare much dried provisions, doubled the march speed at forced pace, and by night reached below the walls.

value.zh: 質明，金鼓聲震地，闔城股栗，遂克之。
value.en: At daybreak, drums and gongs shook the earth; the entire city trembled with fear, and the place was taken.
value.literal: At dawn, drums and gongs shook the earth; the whole city trembled in fear, and they then captured it.

value.zh: 擒其王子別兒怯帖木兒，及偽國公以下三十餘人，收其部落輜重以歸。
value.en: He captured Hami's prince Bie'erqietemür and more than thirty others down to the false state duke, then withdrew with the tribe's baggage train.
value.literal: They captured its prince Bie'erqietemür and more than thirty persons including the false state duke downward; they gathered its tribal baggage and returned.

value.zh: 自是番戎慴服，兵威極於西域。
value.en: From then on the frontier peoples submitted in fear, and Ming military prestige reached its height in the Western Regions.
value.literal: From this the frontier barbarians feared submission, and military awesomeness reached its peak in the Western Regions.

value.zh: 明年五月從藍玉征罕東，徇阿真川，土酋哈昝等遁去。
value.en: The following May he followed Lan Yu on the campaign against Handong, advancing along the Azhen River while native chieftains such as Haza fled.
value.literal: In the fifth month of the next year he followed Lan Yu in campaigning against Handong, marched along Azhen River, and the native chieftains Haza and others fled away.

value.zh: 師還，調中軍都督僉事。
value.en: When the army returned, he was reassigned as assistant regional commander of the Central Army.
value.literal: The army returned; he was transferred to assistant regional commander of the Central Army.

value.zh: 二十八年六月，從總兵官周興出開原，至忽剌江。
value.en: In the sixth month of the twenty-eighth year he joined overall commander Zhou Xing in marching from Kaiyuan to the Hula River.
value.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-eighth year, he followed overall commander Zhou Xing out from Kaiyuan to Hula River.

value.zh: 部長西陽哈遁，追至甫答迷城，俘人畜而還。
value.en: The tribal chief Xiyangha fled; Cheng pursued him to Pudami City, took captives and livestock, and withdrew.
value.literal: The tribal chief Xiyangha fled; pursuing to Pudami City, they took captive people and livestock and returned.

value.zh: 明年拜征南右副將軍，討廣西帡幪諸寨苗，擒斬七千餘人。
value.en: The following year he was appointed Right Vice General for the Southern Expedition and campaigned against Miao stockades at Pingmeng in Guangxi, capturing or killing more than seven thousand.
value.literal: The next year he was appointed Right Vice General for the Southern Expedition, campaigning against the Miao of the various stockades at Pingmeng in Guangxi; captured and beheaded more than seven thousand persons.

value.zh: 又明年，總羽林八衛兵討平五開、龍裏苗。
value.en: The year after that he led the eight Palace Guard garrisons and pacified the Miao of Wukai and Longli.
value.literal: Again the next year, commanding the troops of the eight guards of the Palace Guard, he campaigned to pacify the Miao of Wukai and Longli.

value.zh: 三十一年出鎮開平，從燕王出塞，還城萬全諸衛。
value.en: In the thirty-first year he took command at Kaiping, accompanied the Prince of Yan on a campaign beyond the frontier, and on the return fortified the garrisons at Wanquan.
value.literal: In the thirty-first year he went out to command at Kaiping, followed the Prince of Yan beyond the frontier, and on return walled the various guards at Wanquan.

value.zh: 建文改元，仍鎮甘肅。
value.en: When the Jianwen era began, he continued to hold command in Gansu.
value.literal: When the Jianwen reign era began, he still commanded at Gansu.

value.zh: 成祖即位，入朝，進後軍左都督，拜平羌將軍，遣還鎮。
value.en: After Emperor Chengzu took the throne, he came to court, was promoted to Left Regional Commander of the Rear Army, appointed General Who Pacifies the Qiang, and sent back to his frontier command.
value.literal: When Emperor Chengzu ascended the throne, he entered court, was advanced to Left Regional Commander of the Rear Army, appointed General Who Pacifies the Qiang, and sent back to command.

value.zh: 永樂三年招降把都帖木兒、倫都兒灰等部落五千人，獲馬駝牛羊萬六千。
value.en: In the third year of Yongle he induced five thousand tribesmen under Badutemür, Lundu'erhui, and others to submit, and seized sixteen thousand horses, camels, cattle, and sheep.
value.literal: In the third year of Yongle he induced the surrender of the tribes of Badutemür, Lundu'erhui, and others—five thousand persons—and obtained sixteen thousand horses, camels, cattle, and sheep.

value.zh: 封西寧侯，祿千一百石，世指揮使。
value.en: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xining with an annual stipend of 1,100 shi and the hereditary rank of garrison commander.
value.literal: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xining, with an emolument of 1,100 shi, hereditary garrison commander.

value.zh: 晟凡四鎮涼州，前後二十餘年，威信著絕域。
value.en: In all Cheng held command at Liangzhou four times over more than twenty years, and his prestige reached the farthest frontiers.
value.literal: Cheng altogether four times commanded at Liangzhou; front and back more than twenty years, prestige and authority were renowned in the remote regions.

value.zh: 帝以晟舊臣，有大將材，專任以邊事，所奏請輒報可。
value.en: The emperor, regarding Cheng as a veteran with true generalship, gave him exclusive charge of frontier affairs, and his proposals were invariably approved.
value.literal: The Emperor, because Cheng was an old minister with great general's talent, specially entrusted him with frontier affairs; whatever he memorialized requesting was always approved.

value.zh: 御史劾晟自專。
value.en: A censor impeached Cheng for acting autocratically.
value.literal: A censor impeached Cheng for acting on his own authority.

value.zh: 帝曰：「任人不專則不能成功，況大將統制一邊，寧能盡拘文法。」
value.en: The emperor replied: "If one does not give an appointee full authority, nothing can be accomplished—and when a major general controls an entire frontier, how can he be shackled by every rule in the code?"
value.literal: The Emperor said: "If one does not entrust a man with full authority, success cannot be achieved; moreover, when a great general commands a frontier, how can he be fully bound by written regulations?"

value.zh: 即敕晟以便宜從事。
value.en: He immediately authorized Cheng to act at his discretion as circumstances required.
value.literal: He at once ordered Cheng to act at his discretion as circumstances required.

value.zh: 晟嘗請入朝。
value.en: Cheng once requested leave to come to court.
value.literal: Cheng once requested to enter court.

value.zh: 報曰：「西北邊務，一以委卿，非召命，毋輒來。」
value.en: The reply read: "Northwestern frontier affairs are entirely yours; unless you are summoned, do not come on your own."
value.literal: The reply said: "Northwestern frontier affairs I entirely entrust to you; unless summoned, do not come on your own."

value.zh: 尋命營河西牧地，及圖出塞方略。
value.en: He was soon ordered to develop pasture lands west of the Yellow River and to draft plans for campaigns beyond the frontier.
value.literal: Soon he was ordered to develop pasture lands west of the river and to map plans for campaigns beyond the frontier.

value.zh: 會病卒，五年七月也。
value.en: He then fell ill and died, in the seventh month of the fifth year.
value.literal: He happened to die of illness—it was the seventh month of the fifth year.

value.zh: 晟三子。
value.en: Cheng had three sons.
value.literal: Cheng had three sons.

value.zh: 長瑄，建文中為府軍右衛指揮使，戰靈璧，先登，斬數級，力鬥死。
value.en: The eldest, Xuan, was garrison commander of the Right Guard of the Palace Army during the Jianwen reign. At Lingbi he was first over the wall, killed several enemies, and died fighting.
value.literal: The eldest Xuan, during Jianwen's reign served as garrison commander of the Right Guard of the Palace Army; at the battle of Lingbi he was first to ascend, beheaded several heads, and died fighting with full strength.

value.zh: 瑄弟琥，尚成祖女安成公主，得嗣侯，予世券。
value.en: Xuan's younger brother Hu married Emperor Chengzu's daughter, Princess Ancheng, succeeded to the marquisate, and received a patent of hereditary entitlement.
value.literal: Xuan's younger brother Hu, married Emperor Chengzu's daughter Princess Ancheng, obtained succession to the marquisate, and was granted a patent of hereditary entitlement.

value.zh: 八年佩前將軍印，鎮甘肅。
value.en: In the eighth year he bore the former general's seal and held command in Gansu.
value.literal: In the eighth year he wore the seal of the former general and commanded at Gansu.

value.zh: 十年與李彬捕叛酋老的罕，俘斬甚眾。
value.en: In the tenth year he and Li Bin captured the rebel chieftain Laodehan, taking many prisoners and heads.
value.literal: In the tenth year, together with Li Bin, he captured the rebellious chieftain Laodehan; captives and beheadings were very numerous.

value.zh: 召還。
value.en: He was then recalled.
value.literal: Recalled.

value.zh: 洪熙元年坐不敬奪爵，並削駙馬都尉官。
value.en: In the first year of Hongxi he was stripped of his title for disrespect and also lost his post as Commandant of Attendants-in-Ordinary.
value.literal: In the first year of Hongxi, through disrespect he was stripped of the marquisate and also removed from the office of Commandant of Attendants-in-Ordinary.

value.zh: 宣德中復都尉。
value.en: During the Xuande reign his commandant rank was restored.
value.literal: During Xuande the commandant post was restored.

value.zh: 琥既廢，弟瑛嗣。
value.en: After Hu's deposition, his younger brother Ying succeeded to the title.
value.literal: Hu having been deposed, his younger brother Ying succeeded.

value.zh: 瑛尚鹹寧公主。
value.en: Ying married Princess Xianning.
value.literal: Ying married Princess Xianning.

value.zh: 正統中，歷掌左軍前府事。
value.en: During the Zhengtong reign he successively directed affairs in the Front Office of the Left Army.
value.literal: During Zhengtong, he successively managed the affairs of the Front Office of the Left Army.

value.zh: 瓦剌也先入寇，瑛充總兵官，督大同守將朱冕、石亨等戰陽和，全軍敗沒，瑛及冕皆戰死。
value.en: When Esen of the Oirats invaded, Ying served as overall commander, directing Datong garrison commanders Zhu Mian and Shi Heng in the battle at Yanghe. The entire force was destroyed, and both Ying and Mian were killed.
value.literal: When the Oirat leader Esen invaded, Ying served as overall commander, supervising the Datong garrison commanders Zhu Mian, Shi Heng, and others in battle at Yanghe; the whole army was defeated and destroyed, and both Ying and Mian died in battle.

value.zh: 贈鄆國公，謚忠順。
value.en: He was posthumously ennobled as Duke of Yun with the posthumous title Loyal and Obedient.
value.literal: Posthumously granted Duke of Yun, posthumous title Zhongshun.

value.zh: 子傑嗣。
value.en: His son Jie succeeded him.
value.literal: His son Jie succeeded.

value.zh: 景泰中典禁兵宿衛，以謹慎稱。
value.en: During the Jingtai reign he commanded the palace guard, noted for his careful conduct.
value.literal: During Jingtai he managed the forbidden troops on palace guard duty, renowned for prudence.

value.zh: 卒，子誠嗣。
value.en: On his death his son Cheng succeeded.
value.literal: He died; his son Cheng succeeded.

value.zh: 署右府事，復佩平羌將軍印，鎮甘肅。
value.en: He acted in the Right Office, again bore the seal of General Who Pacifies the Qiang, and held command in Gansu.
value.literal: Acting in the affairs of the Right Office, he again wore the seal of General Who Pacifies the Qiang and commanded at Gansu.

value.zh: 誠有材武，嘗出獵至涼州，遇寇掠牛馬北去。
value.en: Cheng was skilled in arms; once while hunting near Liangzhou he encountered raiders driving stolen cattle and horses northward.
value.literal: Cheng had talent and martial ability; once on a hunting outing he reached Liangzhou, encountered bandits plundering cattle and horses and going north.

value.zh: 誠三矢殪三人，寇驚散，盡驅所掠還。
value.en: Cheng killed three raiders with three arrows; the rest fled in panic, and he recovered all the stolen livestock.
value.literal: Cheng with three arrows killed three men; the bandits startled and scattered, and he drove back all that had been plundered.

value.zh: 九傳至孫裕德，死流寇難。
value.en: After nine generations the line reached his grandson Yude, who was killed in the roving-bandit upheavals.
value.literal: Through nine transmissions to grandson Yude, he died in the calamity of roaming bandits.

value.zh: 南齊書卷四十三‧列傳第二十四
value.en: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 43, Biographies 24
value.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 43, Biographies 24

value.zh: 初，兄朏爲吳興，𤅢於征虜渚送別，朏指𤅢口曰：「此中唯宜飲酒。」
value.en: Earlier, when his elder brother Tiao was leaving for Wuxing, Yao saw him off at Zhengliu Ford; Tiao pointed at Yao's mouth and said, "This is fit for nothing but drinking wine."
value.literal: Earlier, when his elder brother Fei was taking up the post at Wuxing, Yao saw him off at Zhengliu Ford; Fei pointed at Yao's mouth and said: "In this there is only what suits drinking wine."

value.zh: 𤅢建武之初，專以長酣爲事，與劉瑱沈昭略以觴酌交飲，各至數斗。
value.en: At the start of Jianwu, Yao devoted himself to long drinking bouts; with Liu Zhen and Shen Zhaolüe he exchanged cups and drank together, each consuming several dou.
value.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu, Yao devoted himself solely to long drinking as his occupation; with Liu Zhen and Shen Zhaolüe he exchanged cups and drank together, each reaching several dou.

value.zh: 宋建平王景素辟爲南徐州主簿，深見禮遇。
value.en: Jingsu, Prince Jianping of Song, recruited him as Master of Records for Southern Xuzhou and treated him with great respect.
value.literal: Prince Jianping Jingsu of Song invited him as Master of Records for Southern Xuzhou and treated him with deep courtesy.

value.zh: 景素被誅，左右離散，思遠親視殯葬，手種松柏。
value.en: When Jingsu was executed his attendants scattered; Siyuan personally oversaw the funeral and planted pine and cypress with his own hands.
value.literal: When Jingsu was executed his attendants scattered; Siyuan personally oversaw the encoffining and burial and planted pine and cypress with his own hands.

value.zh: 與廬江何昌宇、沛郡劉璡上表理之，事感朝廷。
value.en: Together with He Changyu of Lujiang and Liu Zhen of Pei Commandery he submitted a memorial to clear the prince's name, and the affair moved the court.
value.literal: Together with He Changyu of Lujiang and Liu Zhen of Pei commandery he submitted a memorial to clear the case; the affair moved the court.

value.zh: 景素女廢爲庶人，思遠分衣食以相資贍，年長，爲備笄總，訪求素對，傾家送遣。
value.en: When Jingsu's daughter was reduced to commoner status, Siyuan shared his food and clothing to support her; when she came of age he prepared her hairpin ceremony, sought a suitable husband, and sent her off at the cost of his entire estate.
value.literal: Jingsu's daughter was demoted to commoner status; Siyuan shared food and clothing to support her; when she grew older he prepared her hairpin and coming-of-age rites, sought a suitable match, and sent her off at the cost of his whole household.

value.zh: 南齊書卷第五十五‧列傳第三十六 孝義
value.en: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 55, Biography 36: Filial Piety and Righteous Conduct
value.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 55, Biographies 36: Filial Piety and Righteous Conduct

value.zh: 朱謙之字處光，吳郡錢唐人也。
value.en: Zhu Qianzhi, courtesy name Chuguang, was from Qiantang in Wu commandery.
value.literal: Zhu Qianzhi, courtesy name Chuguang, was a native of Qiantang in Wu commandery.

value.zh: 父昭之，以學解稱於鄉里。
value.en: His father Zhaozhi was renowned in the district for learning.
value.literal: His father Zhaozhi was famed in the village for learning and understanding.

value.zh: 謙之年數歲，所生母亡，昭之假葬田側，為族人朱幼方燎火所焚。
value.en: When Qianzhi was still a child his birth mother died. Zhaozhi had her buried provisionally by the fields, but kinsman Zhu Youfang's brush fire burned the grave.
value.literal: When Qianzhi was only a few years old, his birth mother died; Zhaozhi had her provisionally buried beside the fields, and the grave was burned by a brush fire set by his clansman Zhu Youfang.

value.zh: 同產姉密語之，謙之雖小，便哀戚如持喪。
value.en: His elder sister told him in secret. Though he was still small, he grieved as though in full mourning.
value.literal: His elder sister by the same mother told him in secret; though Qianzhi was small, he grieved as though in mourning.

value.zh: 年長不婚娶。
value.en: When he grew up he never married.
value.literal: When he grew older he did not marry.

value.zh: 永明中，手刃殺幼方，詣獄自繫。
value.en: During Yongming he slew Youfang with his own hand and surrendered himself to prison.
value.literal: During Yongming he killed Youfang with his own hand and went to prison to surrender himself.

value.zh: 縣令申靈勗表上，別駕孔稚珪、兼記室劉璡、司徒左西掾張融牋與刺史豫章王曰：「禮開報仇之典，以申孝義之情；
value.en: Magistrate Shen Lingxu reported the case. Kong Zhigui, Liu Lin, and Zhang Rong wrote to the Prince of Yuzhang, governor of the region: "Ritual law permits vengeance to express filial duty;
value.literal: The Magistrate Shen Lingxu reported upward; the Attendant Counselor Kong Zhigui, Acting Recorder Liu Lin, and Western Section Clerk of the Minister of Works Zhang Rong wrote a memorial to the Governor, the Prince of Yuzhang, saying: "Rites open the statute of vengeance to express filial and righteous feeling;

value.zh: 法斷相殺之條，以表權時之制。
value.en: statutory law forbids killing to uphold the order of the age.
value.literal: law sets the statute against mutual killing to display the expedient regulation of the age.

value.zh: 謙之揮刃斬冤，旣申私禮；
value.en: Qianzhi struck down his enemy and fulfilled his private duty;
value.literal: Qianzhi swung his blade and cut down his enemy, already fulfilling private obligation;

value.zh: 繫頸就死，又明公法。
value.en: he bound himself and submitted to death, thereby honoring public law as well.
value.literal: he bound his neck and submitted to death, thereby also clarifying public law.

value.zh: 今仍殺之，則成當世罪人；
value.en: If he is executed now, the court makes a criminal of him;
value.literal: If he is now still put to death, he becomes a criminal of the age;

value.zh: 宥而活之，即為盛朝孝子。
value.en: if he is pardoned, he becomes a filial son of this flourishing age.
value.literal: if he is pardoned and allowed to live, he becomes a filial son of this flourishing dynasty.

value.zh: 殺一罪人，未足弘憲；
value.en: Executing one man does little to magnify the law;
value.literal: To kill one criminal is not enough to magnify the constitution;

value.zh: 活一孝子，實廣風德。
value.en: sparing one filial son truly broadens moral influence.
value.literal: to spare one filial son truly broadens custom and virtue.

value.zh: 張緒陸澄，是其鄉舊，應具來由。
value.en: Zhang Xu and Lu Cheng, men of his district, should report the full circumstances.
value.literal: Zhang Xu and Lu Cheng are old acquaintances of his village and should set forth the full circumstances.

value.zh: 融等與謙之竝不相識，區區短見，深有恨然。」
value.en: We do not know Qianzhi at all, yet in our limited view we feel deep regret at the case."
value.literal: Rong and the others did not know Qianzhi at all; in our narrow view we deeply regret this."

value.zh: 豫章王言之世祖，時吳郡太守王慈、太常張緒、尚書陸澄竝表論其事，世祖嘉其義，慮相復報，乃遣謙之隨曹虎西行。
value.en: The Prince of Yuzhang reported to Emperor Wu. Administrator Wang Ci, Zhang Xu of the Ministry of Rites, and Lu Cheng of the Ministry of the Interior all memorialized on the case. The emperor admired Qianzhi's conduct but feared further blood feuds, and sent him west with Cao Hu.
value.literal: The Prince of Yuzhang reported this to Emperor Wu; at the time the Administrator of Wu commandery Wang Ci, the Minister of Ceremonies Zhang Xu, and the Minister of the Interior Lu Cheng all memorialized on the matter. Emperor Wu admired his righteousness but feared mutual reprisals, and therefore sent Qianzhi west with Cao Hu.

value.zh: 將發，幼方子惲於津陽門伺殺謙之，謙之之兄選之又刺殺惲，有司以聞。
value.en: As he was about to leave, Youfang's son Yun ambushed and killed Qianzhi at Jinyang Gate. Qianzhi's brother Xuanzhi then stabbed Yun to death. Officials reported the matter.
value.literal: As he was about to depart, Youfang's son Yun lay in wait at Jinyang Gate and killed Qianzhi; Qianzhi's elder brother Xuanzhi in turn stabbed and killed Yun. The authorities reported this.

value.zh: 世祖曰：「此皆是義事，不可問。」
value.en: Emperor Wu said: "These are all acts of righteousness and must not be prosecuted."
value.literal: Emperor Wu said: "These are all matters of righteousness and must not be prosecuted."

value.zh: 悉赦之。
value.en: He pardoned them all.
value.literal: He pardoned them all.

value.zh: 吳興沈顗聞而歎曰：「弟死於孝，兄殉於義。
value.en: Shen Yan of Wuxing sighed and said: "The younger brother died for filial piety; the elder brother gave his life for righteousness.
value.literal: Shen Yan of Wuxing, hearing of it, sighed and said: "The younger brother died for filial piety; the elder brother gave his life for righteousness.

value.zh: 孝友之節，萃此一門。」
value.en: Filial piety and brotherly devotion are gathered in this one family."
value.literal: The virtues of filial piety and brotherly devotion are gathered in this one household."

value.zh: 選之字處林，有志節，著辯相論。
value.en: Xuanzhi, courtesy name Chulin, was a man of resolve and wrote a treatise on physiognomy.
value.literal: Xuanzhi, courtesy name Chulin, had resolve and integrity and wrote Discourse on Distinguishing Physiognomy.

value.zh: 幼時顧歡見而異之，以女妻焉。
value.en: As a youth Gu Huan was impressed by him and gave him his daughter in marriage.
value.literal: In his youth Gu Huan saw him and was struck by him, giving him his daughter in marriage.

value.zh: 官至江夏王參軍。
value.en: He rose to serve as aide to the Prince of Jiangxia.
value.literal: He reached office as Aide to the Prince of Jiangxia.

value.zh: 列傳第二十九
value.en: the twenty-ninth year of Biography
value.literal: Biographies 29

value.zh: 子孺字季幼，幼聰敏，七歲能屬文。
value.en: His son Liu Ru, courtesy name Jiyou, was clever from childhood and at seven could compose prose.
value.literal: His son Ru, courtesy name Jiyou, was clever from childhood and at seven could compose prose.

value.zh: 年十四居喪，毀瘠骨立，宗黨咸異之。
value.en: At fourteen he kept mourning for a parent, wasted to skin and bone, and all his clan marveled at him.
value.literal: At fourteen he kept mourning; wasted to the bone, all his clan marveled at him.

value.zh: 叔父瑱為義興郡，攜以之官，常置坐側，謂賓客曰：「此吾家明珠也。」
value.en: His uncle Zhen was magistrate of Yixing and took him to his post, always seating him at his side. He told guests: "This is the bright pearl of our house."
value.literal: His uncle Zhen was magistrate of Yixing and took him to his post, always seating him at his side; he told guests: "This is the bright pearl of our house."

value.zh: 及長，美風采，性通和，雖家人不見其喜慍。
value.en: When grown, he had a fine bearing and an open, harmonious nature—even his family never saw him show joy or anger.
value.literal: When grown, he had fine bearing; his nature was open and harmonious—even family never saw him show joy or anger.

value.zh: 本州召迎主簿。
value.en: His home province summoned him to serve as Chief Clerk.
value.literal: His home province summoned him as Chief Clerk.

value.zh: 起家中軍法曹行參軍，時鎮軍沈約聞其名，引為主簿，恒與遊宴賦詩，大為約所嗟賞。
value.en: He entered office as Acting Army Controller in the Central Army Legal Bureau. Shen Yue, General Who Pacifies the Army, heard his name and took him as Chief Clerk; they often feasted and composed poetry together, and Yue greatly admired him.
value.literal: He entered office as Acting Army Controller in the Central Army Legal Bureau; at the time General Who Pacifies the Army Shen Yue heard his name and took him as Chief Clerk, often feasting and composing poetry with him—greatly admired by Yue.

value.zh: 累遷太子中舍人。
value.en: He was repeatedly promoted to Attendant in the Crown Prince's household.
value.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Attendant in the Crown Prince's household.

value.zh: 瑱字士溫，繪弟也。
value.en: Liu Zhen, courtesy name Shiwen, was Hui's younger brother.
value.literal: Zhen, courtesy name Shiwen, was Hui's younger brother.

value.zh: 少有行業，文藻、篆隸、丹青並為當世所稱。
value.en: From youth he had good conduct; literature, seal script, clerical script, and painting were all acclaimed in his age.
value.literal: From youth he had good conduct; literature, seal script, clerical script, and painting were all acclaimed in his age.

value.zh: 時有滎陽毛惠遠善畫馬，瑱善畫婦人，並為當世第一。
value.en: At the time Mao Huiyuan of Xingyang was skilled at painting horses and Zhen at painting women—each was first in the age.
value.literal: At the time Mao Huiyuan of Xingyang was skilled at painting horses, Zhen at painting women—both were first in the age.

value.zh: 瑱妹為齊鄱陽王妃，伉儷甚篤。
value.en: Zhen's younger sister was consort to the Princess of Poyang of Qi; husband and wife were deeply devoted.
value.literal: Zhen's younger sister was consort to the Princess of Poyang of Qi; husband and wife were deeply devoted.

value.zh: 王為齊明帝所誅，妃追傷遂成痼疾，醫所不療。
value.en: The prince was executed by Emperor Ming of Qi; the consort grieved until she fell into chronic illness that physicians could not cure.
value.literal: The prince was executed by Emperor Ming of Qi; the consort grieved and became chronically ill, beyond physicians' cure.

value.zh: 有陳郡殷蒨善寫人面，與真不別，瑱令蒨畫王形像，並圖王平生所寵姬共照鏡狀，如欲偶寢。
value.en: Yin Qian of Chen commandery could paint human faces indistinguishable from life. Zhen had Qian paint the prince's likeness together with the prince's favorite concubines gazing in a mirror, as if about to share the bed.
value.literal: Yin Qian of Chen commandery was skilled at painting human faces indistinguishable from life; Zhen had Qian paint the prince's likeness together with the prince's favorite concubines gazing in a mirror as if about to share the bed.

value.zh: 瑱乃密使媼奶示妃，妃視畫仍唾之，因罵云：「故宜其早死」。
value.en: Zhen secretly had a nurse show the consort the painting. She looked at it and spat, cursing: "So it was right that he died early."
value.literal: Zhen secretly had a nurse show the consort; she looked at the painting and spat at it, cursing: "So it was right that he died early."

value.zh: 於是恩情即歇，病亦除差。
value.en: Thereupon affection ceased and the illness was cured.
value.literal: Thereupon affection ceased and the illness was cured.

value.zh: 此姬亦被廢苦，因即以此畫焚之。
value.en: This concubine too had suffered in disgrace and therefore burned the painting.
value.literal: This concubine too had suffered in disgrace and therefore burned the painting.

value.zh: 瑱仕齊，曆尚書吏部郎，義興太守。
value.en: Zhen served Qi, holding posts as Director in the Ministry of Personnel and Administrator of Yixing.
value.literal: Zhen served Qi, holding posts as Director in the Ministry of Personnel and Administrator of Yixing.

value.zh: 先繪卒。
value.en: He died before Hui.
value.literal: He died before Hui.

value.zh: 列傳第五十九
value.en: the 59th year of Biography
value.literal: Biographies number fifty-nine

value.zh: 陳永定中，吏部尚書徐陵領大著作，復引為史佐。
value.en: In the Yongding era Xu Ling, Minister of Personnel, headed the Grand Historiographer's office and again brought Cha in as history assistant.
value.literal: In Chen's Yongding era, Minister of Personnel Xu Ling headed the Grand Historiographer's office and again brought him in as history assistant.

value.zh: 太建初，補宣明殿學士。
value.en: At the beginning of Taijian he was appointed Scholar of the Hall of Illuminated Proclamation.
value.literal: At the beginning of Taijian he was appointed Scholar of the Hall of Illuminated Proclamation.

value.zh: 尋為通直散騎常侍，報聘于周。
value.en: Soon he became Regular Attendant of the Direct and Upright Cavalry and went on a return mission to the Northern Zhou.
value.literal: Soon he was Regular Attendant of the Direct and Upright Cavalry and returned courtesy on a mission to Zhou.

value.zh: 江左耆舊先在關右者，咸相傾慕。
value.en: Elder scholars of the south who were already in the northwest all admired him.
value.literal: Elders of the left of the Yangzi who were already in the Guan west all inclined toward him in admiration.

value.zh: 沛國劉臻竊於公館訪漢書疑事十餘條，並為剖析，皆有經據。
value.en: Liu Zhen of Pei privately raised more than ten doubtful points from the Book of Han at the guest house. Cha analyzed each with canonical grounding.
value.literal: Liu Zhen of Pei, privately at the guest house, inquired about more than ten doubtful points in the Book of Han; Cha analyzed them all, each with canonical grounding.

value.zh: 臻謂所親曰：「名下定無虛士。」
value.en: Zhen told those close to him, "When a name is established, the man behind it is never hollow."
value.literal: Zhen told those close to him: "When the name is settled, there is certainly no empty gentleman."

value.zh: 著西聘道里記。
value.en: He composed a Record of Routes on the Western Mission.
value.literal: He composed a Record of Routes on the Western Mission.

value.zh: 使還，補東宮學士，遷尚書祠部侍郎。
value.en: On his return he was appointed Eastern Palace Scholar and promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat Rites Section.
value.literal: When the mission returned, he was appointed Eastern Palace Scholar and promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat Rites Section.

value.zh: 先主 劉備
value.en: The Former Lord: Liu Bei.
value.literal: The Former Lord Liu Bei.

value.zh: 先主姓劉，諱備，字玄德，涿郡涿縣人，漢景帝子中山靖王勝之後也。
value.en: The Former Lord was Liu Bei, courtesy Xuande, from Zhuo county in Zhuo commandery, a descendant of Han Prince Jing of Zhongshan, Prince Sheng, son of Emperor Jing.
value.literal: The Former Lord’s surname was Liu, his taboo name was Bei, his courtesy name Xuande; he was a man of Zhuo County in Zhuo Commandery; he was a descendant of Prince Jing of Zhongshan Sheng, son of Han Emperor Jing.

value.zh: 勝子貞，元狩六年封涿縣陸城亭侯，坐酎金失侯，因家焉。
value.en: Sheng’s son Liu Zhen received the village fief of Lucheng at Zhuo in the sixth year of Yuanshou, lost his rank over the “ritual gold” affair, and the line then made its home there.
value.literal: Sheng’s son Zhen, in the sixth year of Yuanshou, was enfeoffed village marquis of Lucheng in Zhuo County; he sat guilty of ritual gold and lost the marquisate; therefore the family settled there.

value.zh: 〈典略曰：備本臨邑侯枝屬也。〉
value.en: 〈The Compendium states that Liu Bei sprang from a collateral branch of the marquises of Linyi.〉
value.literal: 〈The Compendium says: Bei was originally a cadet branch of the marquis of Linyi.〉

value.zh: 先主祖雄，父弘，世仕州郡。
value.en: His grandfather Liu Xiong and father Liu Hong had for generations held posts in local government.
value.literal: The Former Lord’s grandfather was Xiong, his father was Hong; for generations they served in prefecture and commandery offices.

value.zh: 雄舉孝廉，官至東郡範令。
value.en: Liu Xiong rose as a filial and incorrupt candidate to magistrate of Fan in Dong commandery.
value.literal: Xiong was recommended as filial and incorrupt; his office reached magistrate of Fan in Dong Commandery.

value.zh: 王蕃字永元，廬江人也。
value.en: Wang Fan, courtesy name Yongyuan, came from Lujiang commandery.
value.literal: Wang Fan, courtesy name Yongyuan, was a man of Lujiang.

value.zh: 博覽多聞，兼通術藝。
value.en: He was widely read and well informed, and equally at home with astronomy, mathematics, and the technical arts.
value.literal: He read widely and heard much, and was also versed in technical arts.

value.zh: 始為尚書郎，去官。
value.en: He began as a gentleman clerk in the secretariat, then resigned his post.
value.literal: At first he was gentleman of the masters of writing, then left office.

value.zh: 孫休即位，與賀邵、薛瑩、虞汜俱為散騎中常侍，皆加駙馬都尉。
value.en: When Sun Xiu took the throne, Wang Fan, He Shao, Xue Ying, and Yu Si were all named attendants at ease and regular palace attendants, each with the additional title chief commandant of carriage escort.
value.literal: When Sun Xiu ascended the throne, together with He Shao, Xue Ying, and Yu Si he became attendant at ease and regular palace attendant, and to each was added chief commandant of carriage escort.

value.zh: 時論清之。
value.en: Public opinion ranked them among the court's clearest spirits.
value.literal: Contemporary opinion deemed them pure.

value.zh: 遣使至蜀，蜀人稱焉，還為夏口監軍。
value.en: Sent on embassy to Shu, he won high praise there; on his return he was named supervisor of the army at Xiakou.
value.literal: He was sent as envoy to Shu; the people of Shu praised him, and on return he became supervisor of the army at Xiakou.

value.zh: 事乎之後，當觀時設制，三王不相因禮，五帝不相沿樂，質文殊塗，損益異體，宜得輩依準古義，有所改立。
value.en: When peace comes you must reform rites and music as kings of old did—let scholars take the classics as your guide.
value.literal: After affairs are settled, one ought to observe the times and set institutions; the three kings did not inherit one another's rites, the five emperors did not continue one another's music—substance and pattern differ in path, decrease and increase differ in body—one ought to get a group to take ancient meaning as standard and have places to change and establish.

value.zh: 漢氏承秦，則有叔孫通定一代之儀，曜之才學亦漢通之次也。
value.en: Wei Yao could be another Shusun Tong for this dynasty.
value.literal: The Han house inherited Qin, then there was Shusun Tong who fixed a generation's observances—Yao's talent and learning are next after Han's Tong.

value.zh: 又《吳書》雖已有頭角，敘贊未述。
value.en: The Book of Wu has a skeleton but lacks full narrative and appraisal.
value.literal: Moreover the Book of Wu, though it already has horns and head, narrative and praise are not yet set forth.

value.zh: 昔班固作《漢書》，文辭典雅，後劉珍，劉毅等作《漢記》，遠不及固，敘傳尤劣。
value.en: Ban Gu's Han shu towers over the Han ji of Liu Zhen, Liu Yi, and others—the latter's biographies are poor stuff.
value.literal: In olden times Ban Gu made the Han shu, literary phrasing classic and elegant; afterward Liu Zhen and Liu Yi and others made the Han ji, far not reaching Gu, especially narrative and biography inferior.

value.zh: 今年《吳書》當垂千載，編次諸吏，後之才士論次善惡，非得良才如曜者，實不可使闕不朽之書。
value.en: The Wu history must last a millennium—without a talent like Wei Yao it cannot be perfected.
value.literal: Now this year the Book of Wu is to hang for a thousand ages; compiling and ordering the various clerks, later men of talent ordering good and evil—if one does not get a good talent like Yao, truly one cannot let the book of indestructibility lack.

value.zh: 如臣頑蔽，誠非其人。
value.en: I am too dull for the task myself.
value.literal: As your servant is stubborn and blocked, truly he is not that man.

value.zh: 文苑四
value.en: Literary Grove, Part Four
value.literal: Literary Grove Four

value.zh: 世言唐所以亡，由諸侯之強，此未極於理。
value.en: The age says Tang perished because the feudatories were strong—this does not reach the limit of reason.
value.literal: The age says Tang perished because the feudatories were strong—this does not reach the limit of reason.

value.zh: 夫弱唐者，諸侯也。
value.en: What weakened Tang were the feudatories.
value.literal: What weakened Tang were the feudatories.

value.zh: 唐既弱矣，而久不亡者，諸侯維之也。
value.en: Once Tang was weak, yet long did not perish because the feudatories sustained it.
value.literal: Once Tang was weak, yet long did not perish because the feudatories sustained it.

value.zh: 燕、趙、魏首亂唐製，專地而治，若古之建國，此諸侯之雄者，然皆恃唐為輕重。
value.en: Yan, Zhao, and Wei first disturbed Tang's system, held territory and governed like ancient states—these were the mighty among feudatories, yet all relied on Tang for weight.
value.literal: Yan, Zhao, and Wei first disturbed Tang's system, held territory and governed like ancient states—these were the mighty among feudatories, yet all relied on Tang for weight.

value.zh: 何則？
value.en: Why?
value.literal: Why?

value.zh: 假王命以相製則易而順，唐雖病之，亦不得而外焉。
value.en: Borrowing the king's mandate to restrain one another was easy and orderly; though Tang was ill, it could not be cast aside.
value.literal: Borrowing the king's mandate to restrain one another was easy and orderly; though Tang was ill, it could not be cast aside.

value.zh: 故河北順而聽命，則天下為亂者不能遂其亂；
value.en: Thus when Hebei was obedient and listened to orders, those who would make trouble in the realm could not complete their trouble;
value.literal: Thus when Hebei was obedient and listened to orders, those who would make trouble in the realm could not complete their trouble;

value.zh: 河北不順而變，則奸雄或附而起。
value.en: when Hebei was disobedient and changed, then treacherous heroes might rise attached.
value.literal: when Hebei was disobedient and changed, then treacherous heroes might rise attached.

value.zh: 德宗世，朱泚、李希烈始遂其僭而終敗亡，田悅叛於前，武俊順於後也。
value.en: In Emperor Dezong's time Zhu Ci and Li Xilie first achieved their usurpation yet finally were defeated; Tian Yue rebelled before, Wu Jun was obedient after.
value.literal: In Emperor Dezong's time Zhu Ci and Li Xilie first achieved their usurpation yet finally were defeated and destroyed; Tian Yue rebelled before, Wu Jun was obedient after.

value.zh: 憲宗討蜀、平夏、誅蔡、夷鄆，兵連四方而亂不生，卒成中興之功者，田氏稟命、王承宗歸國也。
value.en: Emperor Xianzong attacked Shu, pacified Xia, executed Cai, and destroyed Yun; armies linked the four quarters yet disorder did not arise—mid-dynasty revival was because the Tian clan received orders and Wang Chengzong returned to the state.
