value.literal: Emperor Xianzong attacked Shu, pacified Xia, executed Cai, and destroyed Yun; armies linked the four quarters yet disorder did not arise—the merit of mid-dynasty revival was because the Tian clan received orders and Wang Chengzong returned to the state.

value.zh: 武宗將討劉稹之叛，先正三鎮，絕其連衡之計，而王誅以成。
value.en: When Emperor Wuzong was about to attack Liu Zhen's rebellion, he first rectified the three circuits, cut off their alliance plan, and Wang's execution succeeded.
value.literal: When Emperor Wuzong was about to attack Liu Zhen's rebellion, he first rectified the three circuits, cut off their alliance plan, and Wang's execution succeeded.

value.zh: 如是二百年，奸臣逆子專國命者有之，夷將相者有之，而不敢窺神器，非力不足，畏諸侯之勢也。
value.en: Thus for two hundred years wicked ministers and rebellious sons monopolized state power, yet none dared peer at the throne—not from insufficient strength but from fear of the feudatories' power.
value.literal: Thus for two hundred years there were wicked ministers and rebellious sons who monopolized state power and degraded generals and ministers, yet none dared peer at the sacred vessel—not from insufficient strength but from fear of the feudatories' power.

value.zh: 開皇九年，平陳，獲宋、齊舊樂，詔于太常置清商署以管之。
value.en: ninth year of In of Kaihuang, after Chen fell, Song and Qi court music was seized and a Qing Shang Office was set up under the Grand Music Master.
value.literal: In the ninth year of Kaihuang, after the conquest of Chen, the court acquired the old music of Song and Qi; an edict ordered the establishment of a Qing Shang Office under the Director of Ceremonies to administer it.

value.zh: 求陳太樂令蔡子元、於普明等，復居其職。
value.en: Cai Ziyuan, Yu Puming, and other former Chen music officials were found and reappointed.
value.literal: Chen's former Director of Music Cai Ziyuan, Yu Puming, and others were sought out and restored to their posts.

value.zh: 由是牛弘奏曰：
value.en: Niu Hong then submitted a memorial:
value.literal: Thereupon Niu Hong memorialized, saying:

value.zh: 牛弘遂因鄭譯之舊，又請依古五聲六律，旋相為宮。
value.en: Niu Hong, building on Zheng Yi, also asked to restore cyclical palace modulation from the five tones and six pitch-pipes.
value.literal: Niu Hong then, following Zheng Yi's earlier work, also requested that the ancient five tones and six pitch-pipes be used, cyclically modulating as palace keys.

value.zh: 雅樂每宮但一調，唯迎氣奏五調，謂之五音。
value.en: Court music used one mode per palace key; only qi-welcoming rites used five modes—the five tones.
value.literal: In court ritual music each palace key had only one mode; only for welcoming the qi were five modes played—these were called the five tones.

value.zh: 縵樂用七調，祭祀施用。
value.en: Slow ceremonial music used seven modes for sacrifice.
value.literal: Slow music used seven modes and was employed in sacrifices.

value.zh: 各依聲律尊卑為次。
value.en: Each was ranked by pitch hierarchy.
value.literal: Each was ordered according to the rank of pitch and tone.

value.zh: 高祖猶憶妥言，注弘奏下，不許作旋宮之樂，但作黃鐘一宮而已。
value.en: Gaozu heeded Tuo's advice, annotated Niu Hong's memorial, and forbade cyclical modulation—only Yellow Bell palace would do.
value.literal: Gaozu still remembered Tuo's words; he annotated Niu Hong's memorial and rejected cyclical-palace music, allowing only a single Yellow Bell palace key.

value.zh: 於是牛弘及秘書丞姚察、通直散騎常侍許善心、儀同三司劉臻、通直郎虞世基等，更共詳議曰：
value.en: Niu Hong, Yao Cha, Xu Shanxin, Liu Zhen, Yu Shiji, and others then deliberated jointly:
value.literal: Thereupon Niu Hong, Secretariat Aide Yao Cha, Palace Attendant Xu Shanxin, Commissioner Equal to the Three Dukes Liu Zhen, and Secretariat Gentleman Yu Shiji and others jointly deliberated further, saying:

value.zh: 十四年三月，樂定。
value.en: third year of Month, year 14—the music was fixed.
value.literal: Third month of the fourteenth year—the music was fixed.

value.zh: 秘書監、奇章縣公牛弘，秘書丞、北絳郡公姚察，通直散騎常侍、虞部侍郎許善心，兼內史舍人虞世基，儀同三司、東宮學士饒陽伯劉臻等奏曰：「臣聞蕢桴土鼓，由來斯尚，雷出地奮，著自《易經》。
value.en: Niu Hong, Duke of Qizhang County and Director of the Palace Library; Yao Cha, Assistant in the Palace Library and Duke of Beijiang Commandery; Xu Shanxin, Palace Attendant for Unrestricted Communication and Vice Minister of the Bureau of Receptacles; Yu Shiji, concurrently Secretariat Drafter; Liu Zhen, Equal to the Three Excellencies and Eastern Palace scholar, Baron of Raoyang; and others memorialized: "We have heard that rush drumsticks and earthen drums have been honored from antiquity, and that thunder emerging and earth stirring is set forth in the Book of Changes.
value.literal: Secretariat Director and Qizhang County Duke Niu Hong, Secretariat Aide and Beijiang Commandery Duke Yao Cha, Palace Attendant and Yu Department Vice Minister Xu Shanxin, Concurrent Palace Secretariat Gentleman Yu Shiji, Commissioner Equal to the Three Dukes and Eastern Palace Scholar Raoyang Marquis Liu Zhen and others memorialized: "Your subject has heard that earthen drums and earthen drums have been honored from old; thunder emerging from earth and leaping forth is recorded in the Changes.

value.zh: 邃古帝王，經邦馭物，揖讓而臨天下者，祀樂之謂也。
value.en: Ancient emperors governed through sacrificial music.
value.literal: Remote ancient emperors, governing the state and mastering things, yielding the throne and facing all under Heaven—this is what sacrificial music means.

value.zh: 秦焚經典，樂書亡缺，爰至漢興，始加鳩采，祖述增廣，緝成朝憲。
value.en: Qin burned classics; Han began collecting music into court law.
value.literal: Qin burned the classics and music books were lost; only when Han rose did collection begin, inheriting and expanding into court law.

value.zh: 魏、晉相承，更加論討，沿革之宜，備於故實。
value.en: Wei and Jin added discussion recorded in precedent.
value.literal: Wei and Jin handed down and added further discussion—the appropriateness of succession and change is fully recorded in old fact.

value.zh: 永嘉之後，九服崩離，燕、石、苻、姚，遁據華土。
value.en: After Yongjia the realm collapsed; barbarian states held the Central Plains.
value.literal: After Yongjia the nine domains collapsed; Yan, Shi, Fu, and Yao seized and held the Central Plains.

value.zh: 此其戎乎，何必伊川之上，吾其左衽，無復微管之功。
value.en: Barbarians everywhere—not only beyond the Yi; left lapels, no Guan Zhong.
value.literal: These were barbarians—why must it be above the Yi River? Our left lapels—no more Guan Zhong's achievement.

value.zh: 前言往式，於斯而盡。
value.en: Former patterns ended there.
value.literal: The former patterns end here.

value.zh: 金陵建社，朝士南奔，帝則皇規，粲然更備，與內原隔絕，三百年於茲矣。
value.en: Jinling rose; scholars fled south—three centuries cut off from the heartland.
value.literal: Jinling established its altar; court scholars fled south—the imperial regulations brilliantly renewed, yet cut off from the inner heartland for three hundred years.

value.zh: 伏惟明聖膺期，會昌在運。
value.en: Enlightened sagacity received the era; fortune flourishes.
value.literal: Your subject reverently considers that enlightened sagacity received the era; flourishing brilliance is in fortune.

value.zh: 今南征所獲梁、陳樂人，及晉、宋旗章，宛然俱至。
value.en: Liang-Chen musicians and Jin-Song regalia have all arrived.
value.literal: Now musicians of Liang and Chen captured in the southern campaign, and Jin and Song banners and standards, have all duly arrived.

value.zh: 曩代所不服者，今悉服之，前朝所未得者，今悉得之。
value.en: Former non-submitters submit; former lacks are filled.
value.literal: What former ages did not submit to now all submit; what former dynasties did not obtain now all obtain.

value.zh: 化洽功成，於是乎在。
value.en: Transformation harmonized, achievement complete.
value.literal: Transformation harmonized and achievement complete—here it is.

value.zh: 臣等伏奉明詔，詳定雅樂，博訪知音，旁求儒彥，研校是非，定其去就，取為一代正樂，具在本司。」
value.en: We fixed court music as one generation's orthodox repertoire."
value.literal: Your subjects reverently received the clear edict, thoroughly fixing court ritual music, broadly seeking those who know tone, seeking Confucian talents on all sides, examining right and wrong and fixing what to keep or discard, taking this as one generation's orthodox music—all detailed in this office."

value.zh: 於是並撰歌辭三十首，詔並令施用，見行者皆停之。
value.en: Thirty song texts were composed; edict ordered their use and stopped old practice.
value.literal: Thereupon thirty song texts were composed together; an edict ordered all applied, and whatever was in practice was stopped.

value.zh: 其人間音樂，流僻日久，棄其舊體者，並加禁約，務存其本。
value.en: Popular music was restricted to preserve its root.
value.literal: Popular music long flowing in vulgar ways, abandoning its old form—all were restricted to preserve the root.

value.zh: 韋世康，京兆杜陵人也，世為關右著姓。
value.en: Wei Shikang, of Duling in Jingzhao, came from a family that for generations had ranked among the notable surnames of the Guanzhong region.
value.literal: Wei Shikang—Wei Shikang was a native of Duling in Jingzhao; for generations his family had been a prominent clan of the Guanzhong west.

value.zh: 祖旭，魏南幽州刺史。
value.en: His grandfather Xu had served as inspector of Southern Youzhou under the Wei.
value.literal: His grandfather Xu was Southern Youzhou Inspector under the Wei.

value.zh: 父夐，隱居不仕，魏、週二代，十征不出，號為逍遙公。
value.en: His father Jiong had retired from public life; summoned ten times under both Wei and Zhou, he never accepted appointment and was known as the Duke of Leisure.
value.literal: His father Jiong lived in seclusion and did not take office; through the Wei and Zhou dynasties he was summoned ten times and did not emerge, and was styled the Carefree Duke.

value.zh: 世康幼而沉敏，有器度。
value.en: From childhood Shikang was thoughtful and quick-witted, with natural capacity and bearing.
value.literal: Shikang in youth was deep and keen, and had breadth of character.

value.zh: 年十歲，州辟主簿。
value.en: At the age of ten he was recruited by his province as chief clerk.
value.literal: At age ten he was summoned by the province as Registrar.

value.zh: 在魏，弱冠為直寢，封漢安縣公，尚周文帝女襄樂公主，授儀同三司。
value.en: While still young under the Northern Wei he entered the inner guard, was enfeoffed as Duke of Han'an, married Princess Xiangle, daughter of Zhou Emperor Wen, and received the rank of Pillar of State, Third Rank.
value.literal: Under Wei, at weak cap he became Direct Attendant, was enfeoffed as Duke of Han'an, married Princess Xiangle, daughter of Emperor Wen of Zhou, and was appointed Pillar of State, Third Rank.

value.zh: 後仕周，自典祠下大夫曆沔、硤二州刺史。
value.en: He later served the Zhou, advancing from lower grand master of sacrifices to governor in turn of Mian and Qia.
value.literal: Later he served Zhou, rising from Lower Grand Master of Sacrifices through the prefectures of Mian and Qia.

value.zh: 從武帝平齊，授司州總管長史。
value.en: When Emperor Wu conquered Qi, he was made chief administrator on the staff of the Si Province commissioner-general.
value.literal: Following Emperor Wu in the pacification of Qi, he was appointed Chief Administrator to the Commissioner-General of Si Province.

value.zh: 于時東夏初定，百姓未安，世康綏撫之，士民胥悅。
value.en: The east had only just been pacified and the populace was still unsettled; Shikang reassured them until officials and people alike were content.
value.literal: At that time the eastern regions had just been settled and the people were not yet at peace; Shikang soothed them, and gentry and commoners alike rejoiced.

value.zh: 歲餘，入為民部中大夫，進位上開府，轉司會中大夫。
value.en: A year later he was recalled to court as grand master of the ministry of the people, promoted to upper pillar of state, and then transferred to grand master of the department of accounts.
value.literal: After more than a year he entered the capital as Grand Master of the Ministry of the People, advanced to Upper Pillar of State, and transferred to Grand Master of the Department of Accounts.

value.zh: 初，機在周，與族人文城公昂俱曆顯要。
value.en: In Zhou days he and his kinsman Duke Ang of Wencheng had both held high office.
value.literal: Earlier, when Ji was in Zhou, he together with his clansman the Duke of Wencheng Ang both held prominent posts.

value.zh: 及此，機、昂並為外職，楊素時為納言，方用事，因上賜宴，素戲機曰：「二柳俱摧，孤楊獨聳。」
value.en: Now Ji and Ang served in the provinces while Yang Su, chamberlain and favorite, jested at court: "Both willows are broken; the lone poplar stands tall."
value.literal: By this time Ji and Ang were both in outer posts; Yang Su at the time was Chamberlain and just then wielded power—therefore at an imperial feast Su jested to Ji: "Both willows are broken down; the lone poplar stands tall alone."

value.zh: 坐者歡笑，機竟無言。
value.en: The company laughed; Ji said nothing.
value.literal: Those seated laughed; Ji in the end had no words.

value.zh: 未幾，還州。
value.en: He soon returned to his province.
value.literal: Before long he returned to his province.

value.zh: 前後作牧，俱稱寬惠。
value.en: As regional governor he was always praised for lenient rule.
value.literal: Before and after as governor he was all called generous and kind.

value.zh: 後數年，以疾征還京師，卒于家，時年五十六。
value.en: Years later, recalled ill, he died at home at fifty-six.
value.literal: Several years later, because of illness he was summoned back to the capital and died at home, aged fifty-six.

value.zh: 贈大將軍、青州刺史，諡曰簡。
value.en: He was posthumously made grand general and prefect of Qing with the temple name Jian.
value.literal: Posthumously made Grand General and Prefect of Qing, with posthumous title Jian.

value.zh: 子述嗣。
value.en: His son Shu succeeded him.
value.literal: His son Shu succeeded.

value.zh: 子述柳述，字業隆，性明敏，有幹略，頗涉文藝。
value.en: Shu, styled Yelong, was clever, capable, and accomplished in letters.
value.literal: Shu—Liu Shu styled Yelong—was by nature bright and keen, had capacity and strategy, and was quite versed in literary arts.

value.zh: 少以父廕，為太子親衛。
value.en: Through his father's privilege he became a close guard of the heir apparent.
value.literal: In youth through his father's shade he became Close Guard of the Heir Apparent.

value.zh: 後以尚主之故，拜開府儀同三司、內史侍郎。
value.en: Marriage to an imperial princess brought him pillar of state with insignia of office and vice director of the secretariat.
value.literal: Later because of marrying the princess he was appointed Pillar of State with the insignia of office, Third Rank, and Secretariat Vice Director.

value.zh: 上于諸婿中，特所寵敬。
value.en: Among the imperial sons-in-law the emperor favored and respected him above the rest.
value.literal: Among all the sons-in-law the emperor especially favored and respected him.

value.zh: 歲餘，判兵部尚書事。
value.en: A year later he was given concurrent charge of the ministry of war.
value.literal: After more than a year he concurrently judged Ministry of War affairs.

value.zh: 丁父艱去職。
value.en: He resigned to observe mourning for his father.
value.literal: He left office on mourning for his father.

value.zh: 未幾，起攝給事黃門侍郎事，襲爵建安郡公。
value.en: He was soon recalled as acting vice director of the yellow gate and inherited the dukedom of Jian'an.
value.literal: Before long he was recalled to act as Attendant of the Yellow Gate and Vice Director, inheriting the noble rank Duke of Jian'an.

value.zh: 仁壽中，判吏部尚書事。
value.en: During Renshou he was given concurrent charge of the civil service ministry.
value.literal: In Renshou he concurrently judged Ministry of the Civil Service affairs.

value.zh: 述雖職務修理，為當時所稱，然不達大體，暴於馭下，又怙寵驕豪，無所降屈。
value.en: Though efficient and praised at court, he lacked breadth of vision, bullied subordinates, and grew arrogant on imperial favor.
value.literal: Though Shu's duties were well ordered and praised in the age, he did not comprehend the larger pattern, was harsh in controlling subordinates, and also relied on favor and was arrogant and overbearing, bowing to no one.

value.zh: 楊素時稱貴幸，朝臣莫不讋憚，述每陵侮之，數於上前面折素短。
value.en: Yang Su then dominated the court, yet Shu repeatedly humiliated him and exposed his faults before the emperor.
value.literal: Yang Su at the time was called honored and favored; court ministers all feared him—Shu each time insulted him and several times before the emperor exposed Su's faults.

value.zh: 判事有不合素意，素或令述改之，輒謂將命者曰：「語僕射，道尚書不肯。」
value.en: When Su ordered him to alter a decision Shu refused, telling the messenger, "Tell the Vice Director the Minister will not."
value.literal: When judging affairs did not accord with Su's intent, Su sometimes ordered Shu to change them; he would tell the bearer of orders: "Tell the Vice Director—the Minister says he will not."

value.zh: 素由是銜之。
value.en: Su therefore nursed a grievance against him.
value.literal: Su thereby bore a grudge.

value.zh: 俄而楊素亦被疏忌，不知省務。
value.en: Soon Yang Su too fell from favor and neglected his duties.
value.literal: Shortly Yang Su was also distanced and suspected, not knowing provincial affairs.

value.zh: 述任寄逾重，拜兵部尚書，參掌機密。
value.en: Shu's responsibilities grew; he became minister of war and shared state secrets.
value.literal: Shu's commission grew heavier; he was appointed Minister of War and shared in confidential matters.

value.zh: 述自以無功可紀，過叨匪服，抗表陳讓。
value.en: Believing he had no merit for such rank, he petitioned to resign.
value.literal: Shu himself thought he had no merit to record and had excessively received unfitting rank; he submitted a memorial firmly declining.

value.zh: 上許之，令攝兵部尚書事。
value.en: The emperor agreed and had him act as minister of war.
value.literal: The emperor permitted it and ordered him to act as Minister of War.

value.zh: 上于仁壽宮寢疾，述與楊素、黃門侍郎元岩等侍疾宮中。
value.en: When the emperor fell ill at Renshou Palace, Shu attended him with Yang Su and Yuan Yan.
value.literal: When the emperor lay ill at Renshou Palace, Shu together with Yang Su, Yellow Gate Attendant Yuan Yan, and others attended the illness in the palace.

value.zh: 時皇太子無禮于陳貴人，上知而大怒，因令述召房陵王。
value.en: Learning the crown prince had insulted Lady Chen, the emperor angrily ordered Shu to summon Prince Yong of Fangling.
value.literal: At that time the Crown Prince was disrespectful to Lady Chen; when the emperor knew he was greatly angry and ordered Shu to summon the Prince of Fangling.

value.zh: 述與元岩出外作敕書，楊素聞之，與皇太子協謀，便矯詔執述、岩二人，持以屬吏。
value.en: Shu and Yuan Yan went out to draft the edict; Yang Su conspired with the crown prince, forged orders, and had them arrested.
value.literal: Shu and Yuan Yan went outside to draft the edict; Yang Su heard and conspired with the Crown Prince, then forged an edict to arrest Shu and Yan and hand them to the officials.

value.zh: 及煬帝嗣位，述竟坐除名，與公主離絕。
value.en: When Emperor Yang succeeded, Shu was dismissed and separated from the princess.
value.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded, Shu was dismissed for the offense and separated from the princess.

value.zh: 徙述于龍川郡。
value.en: He was exiled to Longchuan.
value.literal: Shu was banished to Longchuan commandery.

value.zh: 公主請與述同徙，帝不聽，事見《列女傳》。
value.en: The princess asked to share his exile; the emperor refused—the account appears in the 《Biographies of Exemplary Women》.
value.literal: The princess requested to be banished with Shu; the emperor did not listen—the matter is recorded in the "Biographies of Exemplary Women" (Lie nü zhuan).

value.zh: 述在龍川數年，複徙寧越，遇瘴癘而死，時年三十九。
value.en: After years in Longchuan he was moved to Ningyue, where miasma killed him at thirty-nine.
value.literal: After several years in Longchuan he was again banished to Ningyue; encountering miasma he died, aged thirty-nine.

value.zh: 弟旦旦字匡德，工騎射，頗涉書籍。
value.en: His younger brother Dan, styled Kuangde, excelled at horsemanship and archery and was well read.
value.literal: Younger brother Dan—Dan styled Kuangde—was skilled at mounted archery and quite versed in books.

value.zh: 起家周左侍上士，累遷兵部下大夫。
value.en: He entered service under the Zhou as left attendant upper gentleman and rose to lower grand master of war.
value.literal: He began his career as Zhou Left Attendant Upper Gentleman and was repeatedly promoted to Lower Grand Master of War.

value.zh: 頃之，益州總管王謙起逆，拜為行軍長史，從梁睿討平之，以功授儀同三司。
value.en: When Wang Qian of Yi rebelled he served as campaign chief administrator under Liang Rui and was made pillar of state, third rank.
value.literal: Shortly Commissioner-General Wang Qian of Yi rose in rebellion; he was appointed Campaign Chief Administrator and followed Liang Rui in suppressing and pacifying him; for merit he was appointed Pillar of State, Third Rank.

value.zh: 開皇元年，加授開府，封新城縣男，遷授掌設驃騎。
value.en: In Kaihuang year one he was made pillar of state, enfeoffed Baron of Xincheng, and given command of the setting pillar of cavalry.
value.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang he was additionally appointed Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Baron of Xincheng, and transferred to command the Setting Pillar of Cavalry.

value.zh: 曆羅、淅、魯三州刺史，並有能名。
value.en: He governed Luo, Xi, and Lu in turn, all with a reputation for competence.
value.literal: He served in succession as Prefect of Luo, Xi, and Lu—all had reputation for ability.

value.zh: 大業初，拜龍川太守。
value.en: At the start of Daye he was made prefect of Longchuan.
value.literal: At the beginning of Daye he was appointed Prefect of Longchuan.

value.zh: 民居山洞，好相攻擊，旦為開設學校，大變其風。
value.en: The people lived in mountain caves and raided one another until Dan founded schools and transformed their ways.
value.literal: The people lived in mountain caves and loved to attack one another; Dan established schools and greatly changed their customs.

value.zh: 帝聞而善之，下詔褒美。
value.en: The emperor praised him in an edict.
value.literal: When the emperor heard he approved and issued an edict praising him.

value.zh: 四年，征為太常少卿，攝判黃門侍郎事。
value.en: In year four he was recalled as vice minister of imperial sacrifices and acting vice director of the yellow gate.
value.literal: In the fourth year he was summoned as Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices and acted as Concurrent Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.

value.zh: 卒官，年六十一。
value.en: He died in office at sixty-one.
value.literal: He died in office, aged sixty-one.

value.zh: 子燮，官至河內掾。
value.en: His son Xie rose to administrator of Henei.
value.literal: His son Xie reached the office of Administrator of Henei.

value.zh: 旦弟肅肅字匡仁，少聰敏，閑於占對。
value.en: Dan's younger brother Su, styled Kuangren, was clever and quick in debate from youth.
value.literal: Dan's younger brother Su—Su styled Kuangren—in youth was clever and keen, skilled in repartee.

value.zh: 起家周齊王文學。
value.en: He began under the Zhou as literary scholar to Prince Wen of Qi.
value.literal: He began his career as Literary Scholar to Prince Wen of Qi under the Zhou.

value.zh: 武帝見而異之，召拜宣納上士。
value.en: Zhou Emperor Wu was impressed and appointed him upper gentleman of the secretariat.
value.literal: Emperor Wu saw him and was struck by him; he was summoned and appointed Upper Gentleman of the Secretariat.

value.zh: 高祖作相，引為賓曹參軍。
value.en: When Gaozu became chancellor he was made guest army officer.
value.literal: When Gaozu became Chancellor he was drawn as Guest Army Officer.

value.zh: 開皇初，授太子洗馬。
value.en: In early Kaihuang he became crown prince libationer.
value.literal: In early Kaihuang he was appointed Crown Prince Libationer.

value.zh: 陳使謝泉來聘，以才學見稱，詔肅宴接，時論稱其華辯。
value.en: When the Chen envoy Xie Quan came, Su was ordered to entertain him and was praised for eloquence.
value.literal: When Chen envoy Xie Quan came on a mission, because of literary talent he was praised; an edict ordered Su to entertain him—opinion of the time called his brilliance and eloquence.

value.zh: 轉太子內舍人，遷太子僕。
value.en: He became crown prince inner attendant, then crown prince steward.
value.literal: He transferred to Crown Prince Inner Attendant and was promoted Crown Prince Steward.

value.zh: 太子廢，坐除名為民。
value.en: When the crown prince was deposed he was reduced to commoner status.
value.literal: When the Crown Prince was deposed he sat for dismissal and was made a commoner.

value.zh: 大業中，帝與段達語及庶人罪惡之狀，達雲：「柳肅在宮，大見疏斥。」
value.en: In Daye the emperor discussed the deposed heir with Duan Da, who said, "Liu Su had been greatly slighted in the palace."
value.literal: In Daye the emperor spoke with Duan Da about the deposed heir's wicked conduct; Da said: "Liu Su in the palace was greatly slighted and rejected."

value.zh: 帝問其故，答曰：「學士劉臻，嘗進章仇太翼于宮中，為巫蠱事。
value.en: The emperor asked why. Duan Da answered, "The scholar Liu Zhen once brought Zhang Qiu Taiyi into the palace for sorcery.
value.literal: The emperor asked the reason; he answered: "Scholar Liu Zhen once introduced Zhang Qiu Taiyi into the palace for witchcraft affairs.

value.zh: 肅知而諫曰：'殿下帝之塚子，位當儲貳，誡在不孝，無患見疑。
value.en: Su warned, "You are the emperor's heir—beware unfilial conduct, not suspicion."
value.literal: Su knew and remonstrated: "Your Highness is the emperor's heir by tomb and shrine; your station should be heir apparent—caution lies in unfilial conduct, not in being suspected.

value.zh: 劉臻書生，鼓搖脣舌，適足以相誑誤，願殿下勿納之。
value.en: Liu Zhen is a scholar who wags his tongue—do not heed him.
value.literal: Liu Zhen is a bookish man who wags his lips and tongue—he is fit only to deceive and mislead; I beg Your Highness not to accept him."

value.zh: '庶人不懌，他日謂臻曰：'汝何故漏泄，使柳肅知之，令面折我？
value.en: The deposed heir was displeased and later demanded of Zhen, "Why did you leak this so Liu Su could rebuke me to my face?"
value.literal: The deposed heir was displeased and another day said to Zhen: "Why did you leak it and let Liu Su know, making him rebuke me to my face?

value.zh: '自是後言皆不用。」
value.en: After that his counsel went unheeded."
value.literal: From then on his words were not heeded."

value.zh: 帝曰：「肅橫除名，非其罪也。」
value.en: The emperor said, "Su was wrongly dismissed—it was not his fault."
value.literal: The emperor said: "Su was rashly removed from the rolls—not his crime."

value.zh: 召守禮部侍郎，轉工部侍郎，大見親任。
value.en: He was recalled as vice minister of rites, then works, and greatly trusted.
value.literal: He was summoned to act as Vice Minister of Rites, transferred to Vice Minister of Works, and greatly trusted.

value.zh: 每行幸遼東，常委之于涿郡留守。
value.en: On each Liaodong campaign he left Su as guardian at Zhuo.
value.literal: Whenever the emperor campaigned in Liaodong he repeatedly entrusted him to remain and guard at Zhuo.

value.zh: 十一年卒，時年六十二。
value.en: In year eleven he died at sixty-two.
value.literal: In the eleventh year he died, aged sixty-two.

value.zh: 從弟雄亮雄亮字信誠。
value.en: His paternal cousin Xiongliang, styled Xincheng.
value.literal: Paternal cousin Xiongliang—Xiongliang styled Xincheng.

value.zh: 父檜，仕周華陽太守。
value.en: His father Hui was prefect of Huayang under the Zhou.
value.literal: Father Hui served as Zhou Prefect of Huayang.

value.zh: 遇黃眾寶作亂，攻陷華陽，檜為賊所害。
value.en: When Huang Zhongbao rebelled and took Huayang, Hui was killed.
value.literal: Encountering Huang Zhongbao's rebellion, Huayang was attacked and taken; Hui was killed by the bandits.

value.zh: 雄亮時年十四，哀毀過禮，陰有復仇之志。
value.en: Xiongliang was fourteen; his mourning exceeded propriety and he secretly vowed revenge.
value.literal: Xiongliang was then fourteen; his grief and destruction exceeded the rites, and secretly he had the will to take revenge.

value.zh: 武帝時，眾寶率其所部歸於長安，帝待之甚厚。
value.en: Later Zhongbao submitted to Chang'an and was generously treated by Emperor Wu.
value.literal: In Emperor Wu's time Zhongbao led his followers in submission to Chang'an; the emperor treated him very generously.

value.zh: 雄亮手斬眾寶於城中，請罪闕下，帝特原之。
value.en: Xiongliang slew Zhongbao in the city and surrendered for punishment; the emperor pardoned him.
value.literal: Xiongliang with his own hand beheaded Zhongbao in the city and requested punishment below the gate; the emperor specially pardoned him.

value.zh: 尋治梁州總管記室，遷湖城令，累遷內史中大夫，賜爵汝陽縣子。
value.en: He served as recorder on the Liang commissioner-general's staff, then magistrate of Hucheng, then secretariat grand master and Viscount of Ruyang.
value.literal: Soon he managed the records office of the Liang Region Commissioner-General, transferred to Magistrate of Hucheng, and was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of the Secretariat, enfeoffed as Viscount of Ruyang.

value.zh: 司馬消難作亂江北，高祖令雄亮聘于陳，以結鄰好。
value.en: When Sima Xiaonan rebelled, Gaozu sent him to Chen to secure an alliance.
value.literal: When Sima Xiaonan rebelled north of the river, Gaozu ordered Xiongliang to go on mission to Chen to secure neighborly good relations.

value.zh: 及還，會高祖受禪，拜尚書考功侍郎，尋遷給事黃門侍郎。
value.en: On his return Gaozu had taken the throne; he became vice director for merit evaluation, then yellow gate attendant.
value.literal: When he returned, Gaozu had received the abdication; he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat for Merit Evaluation and soon transferred to Attendant of the Yellow Gate.

value.zh: 尚書省凡有奏事，雄亮多所駁正，深為公卿所憚。
value.en: He often rejected Secretariat memorials and was feared by the ministers.
value.literal: Whenever the Secretariat had memorials to present, Xiongliang many times rejected and corrected them, and the public ministers deeply feared him.

value.zh: 俄以本官檢校太子左庶子，進爵為伯。
value.en: He was soon made acting left heir apparent of the crown prince and raised to earl.
value.literal: Shortly with his original office he inspected and acted as Left Heir Apparent of the Crown Prince, advanced in noble rank to Earl.

value.zh: 秦王俊之鎮隴右也，出為秦州總管府司馬，領山南道行台左丞，卒官，時年五十一。
value.en: When Prince Jun of Qin went to Longyou he served as his chief administrator and south mountain route assistant until he died at fifty-one.
value.literal: When Prince of Qin Jun went to secure Longyou he went out as Chief Administrator of the Qin Region Commissioner-General's office, concurrently Left Assistant of the South Mountain Route Campaign Headquarters—he died in office, aged fifty-one.

value.zh: 有子贊。
value.en: He had a son Zan.
value.literal: He had a son Zan.

value.zh: 從子謇之謇之字公正。
value.en: His nephew Jianzhi, styled Gongzheng.
value.literal: Nephew Jianzhi—Jianzhi styled Gongzheng.

value.zh: 父蔡年，周順州刺史。
value.en: His father Cai'nian was prefect of Shun under the Zhou.
value.literal: Father Cai'nian was Zhou Prefect of Shun.

value.zh: 謇之身長七尺五寸，儀容甚偉，風神爽亮，進止可觀。
value.en: Jianzhi stood seven feet five inches, imposing in bearing and graceful in movement.
value.literal: Jianzhi's body was seven feet five inches; his bearing was very imposing, his spirit bright and clear, his advance and stop worth viewing.

value.zh: 為童兒時，周齊王憲嘗遇謇之於途，異而與語，大奇之。
value.en: As a boy he met Prince Xian of Qi, who was astonished and recommended him.
value.literal: As a child, Prince Xian of Qi of Zhou once met Jianzhi on the road, was struck by him and conversed—he greatly marveled.

value.zh: 因奏入國子，以明經擢第，拜宗師中士，尋轉守廟下士。
value.en: He entered the imperial academy, passed the classics examination, and became master of the imperial clan.
value.literal: He therefore memorialized entry into the Imperial Academy; through the classics examination he was selected, appointed Master of the Imperial Clan, and soon transferred to Lower Gentleman Guarding the Temple.

value.zh: 武帝嘗有事太廟，謇之讀祝文，音韻清雅，觀者屬目。
value.en: Reading prayers at the Grand Temple with clear, elegant delivery, he drew every eye.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu once had business at the Grand Temple, Jianzhi read the prayer text with clear and elegant tone and pitch—observers fixed their eyes on him.

value.zh: 帝善之，擢為宣納上士。
value.en: The emperor was pleased and made him upper gentleman of the secretariat.
value.literal: The emperor approved and promoted him to Upper Gentleman of the Secretariat.

value.zh: 及高祖作相，引為田曹參軍，仍諮典簽事。
value.en: When Gaozu became chancellor he became field army officer and registry adviser.
value.literal: When Gaozu became Chancellor he was drawn as Field Army Officer and still consulted on registry affairs.

value.zh: 開皇初，拜通事舍人，尋遷內史舍人，曆兵部、司勳二曹侍郎。
value.en: In early Kaihuang he was communications attendant, then secretariat attendant, then vice director of war and merit.
value.literal: In early Kaihuang he was appointed Communications Attendant and soon transferred to Secretariat Attendant, serving in succession as Vice Director of War and Vice Director of Merit.

value.zh: 朝廷以謇之有雅望，善談謔，又飲酒至石不亂，由是每梁、陳使至，輒令謇之接對。
value.en: The court valued his wit and his capacity to drink a stone of wine without disorder, and always sent him to receive Liang and Chen envoys.
value.literal: The court because Jianzhi had refined standing, was skilled in wit, and also could drink to a stone measure without disorder—therefore whenever Liang or Chen envoys arrived they always ordered Jianzhi to receive them.

value.zh: 後遷光祿少卿。
value.en: He was later made vice minister of the imperial household.
value.literal: Later he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Imperial Household.

value.zh: 出入十餘年，每參掌敷奏。
value.en: For more than ten years he helped draft and present memorials.
value.literal: Entering and leaving over more than ten years, each time he shared in drafting and presenting memorials.

value.zh: 會吐谷渾來降，朝廷以宗女光化公主妻之，以謇之兼散騎常侍，送公主于西域。
value.en: When Tuyuhun submitted, he escorted Princess Guanghua west as concurrent regular attendant.
value.literal: When Tuyuhun came to submit, the court married the imperial clan daughter Princess Guanghua to them and made Jianzhi Concurrent Regular Attendant to escort the princess to the Western Regions.

value.zh: 俄而突厥啟民可汗求結和親，複令謇之送義成公主于突厥。
value.en: When the Türk Qimin Qaghan sought alliance he escorted Princess Yicheng to the Türks.
value.literal: Shortly the Tujue Qimin Qaghan sought marriage alliance; again Jianzhi was ordered to escort Princess Yicheng to the Tujue.

value.zh: 謇之前後奉使，得二國所贈馬千餘匹，雜物稱是，皆散之宗族，家無餘財。
value.en: On both missions he received over a thousand horses and gave everything to his kin, leaving nothing at home.
value.literal: Jianzhi on former and latter missions received over a thousand horses from the two states and miscellaneous goods in proportion—all he distributed to his clan; the family had no surplus wealth.

value.zh: 仁壽中，出為肅州刺史，尋轉息州刺史，俱有惠政。
value.en: In Renshou he governed Su, then Xi, both with benevolent rule.
value.literal: In Renshou he went out as Prefect of Su and soon transferred to Prefect of Xi—in both he had benevolent government.

value.zh: 後二歲，以母憂去職。
value.en: Two years later he resigned to mourn his mother.
value.literal: Two years later he left office on mourning for his mother.

value.zh: 煬帝踐阼，複拜光祿少卿。
value.en: When Emperor Yang succeeded he was again made vice minister of the imperial household.
value.literal: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne he was again appointed Vice Minister of the Imperial Household.

value.zh: 大業初，啟民可汗自以內附，遂畜牧於定襄、馬邑間，帝使謇之諭令出塞。
value.en: In early Daye Qimin pastured near the border; the emperor sent Jianzhi to order him beyond the frontier.
value.literal: At the beginning of Daye, Qimin Qaghan because he had submitted inward pastured between Dingxiang and Mayi; the emperor sent Jianzhi to instruct him to go beyond the passes.

value.zh: 及還，奏事稱旨，拜黃門侍郎。
value.en: His report pleased the emperor and he was made yellow gate vice director.
value.literal: When he returned his memorial answered the purpose and he was appointed Yellow Gate Vice Director.

value.zh: 時元德太子初薨，朝野注望，皆以齊王當立。
value.en: When Crown Prince Yuande died, all expected Prince Qi to succeed.
value.literal: At that time the Yuande Crown Prince had just died; court and countryside fixed their hopes—all thought the Prince of Qi would be established.

value.zh: 帝方重王府之選，大業三年，車駕還京師，拜為齊王長史。
value.en: In Daye year three the emperor made him chief administrator to Prince Qi.
value.literal: The emperor was then weighting selections for the princely household; in the third year of Daye when the imperial carriage returned to the capital he was appointed Chief Administrator to the Prince of Qi.

value.zh: 帝法服臨軒，備儀衛，命齊王立於西朝堂之前，北面。
value.en: In full ritual the emperor had Prince Qi stand before the western court hall facing north.
value.literal: The emperor in ritual robes faced the hall, fully arrayed guards of honor, and ordered the Prince of Qi to stand before the western court hall, facing north.

value.zh: 遣吏部尚書牛弘、內史令楊約、左衛大將軍宇文述等，從殿廷引謇之詣齊王所，西面立。
value.en: Niu Hong, Yang Yue, and Yuwen Shu led Jianzhi to stand before the prince facing west.
value.literal: He sent Minister of the Civil Service Niu Hong, Secretariat Director Yang Yue, Left Guard Grand General Yuwen Shu, and others from the hall to lead Jianzhi to the Prince of Qi's place, standing facing west.

value.zh: 牛弘宣敕謂齊王曰：「我昔階緣恩寵，啟封晉陽，出籓之初，時年十二。
value.en: Niu Hong proclaimed to Prince Qi, "Through imperial favor I was once enfeoffed at Jinyang; when I first went to my fief I was only twelve years old.
value.literal: Niu Hong proclaimed the edict to the Prince of Qi: "I formerly through favor of fate was enfeoffed at Jinyang; when I first went out to the frontier I was twelve years old.

value.zh: 先帝立我於西朝堂，乃令高熲、虞慶則、元旻等，從內送王子相于我。
value.en: The former emperor had Gao Feng and others present Prince Xiang to me as companion.
value.literal: The former emperor established me at the western court hall and ordered Gao Feng, Yu Qingze, Yuan Min, and others from within to send Prince Xiang to me.

value.zh: 于時誡我曰：'以汝幼沖，未更世事，今令子相作輔於汝，事無大小，皆可委之。
value.en: He warned me, "You are young—in all matters great or small entrust them to Xiang."
value.literal: At that time he admonished me: "Because you are young and have not yet experienced worldly affairs, I now make Xiang your companion—in affairs great or small you may all entrust them to him.

value.zh: 無得昵近小人，疏遠子相。
value.en: Do not favor petty men or distance yourself from Xiang.
value.literal: Do not draw near petty men or distance yourself from Xiang.

value.zh: 若從我言者，有益於社稷，成立汝名行。
value.en: If you heed this it will benefit the realm and your reputation.
value.literal: If you follow my words it will benefit the altars of soil and grain and establish your name and conduct.

value.zh: 如不用此言，唯國及身，敗無日矣。
value.en: If you ignore it, ruin will come swiftly to you and the state.
value.literal: If you do not use these words, only the state and your person—ruin will be without delay.

value.zh: '吾受敕之後，奉以周旋，不敢失墜。
value.en: I have kept this counsel ever since.
value.literal: After I received the edict I held to it in all dealings and did not dare lose it.

value.zh: 微子相之力，吾無今日矣。
value.en: Without Xiang I would not be emperor today.
value.literal: Without the strength of Xiang I would have no today.

value.zh: 若與謇之從事，一如子相也。」
value.en: Treat Jianzhi as you would Xiang."
value.literal: If you work with Jianzhi, it is just like Xiang."

value.zh: 又敕謇之曰：「今以卿作輔于齊，善思匡救之理，副朕所望。
value.en: He charged Jianzhi, "Serve Qi as Xiang served me—fulfill my hope.
value.literal: Again he charged Jianzhi: "Now I make you companion to Qi—think well on the principle of aiding and saving; match what I hope.

value.zh: 若齊王德業修備，富貴自當鐘卿一門。
value.en: If Qi cultivates virtue, your whole house will prosper.
value.literal: If the Prince of Qi's virtue and enterprise are cultivated and complete, wealth and honor will naturally be heaped on your whole house.

value.zh: 若有不善，罪亦相及。」
value.en: If he errs, you will share the guilt."
value.literal: If there is what is not good, guilt will also reach you."

value.zh: 時齊王正擅寵，左右放縱，喬令則之徒，深見昵狎。
value.en: Prince Qi then held favor and his intimates, including Qiao Lingze, ran wild.
value.literal: At that time the Prince of Qi was just then monopolizing favor; his close attendants were unrestrained—men like Qiao Lingze were deeply drawn near and pampered.

value.zh: 謇之雖知其罪失，不能匡正。
value.en: Jianzhi knew their faults but could not correct them.
value.literal: Jianzhi though he knew their faults and errors could not correct and straighten them.

value.zh: 及王得罪，謇之竟坐除名。
value.en: When Prince Qi fell from favor, Jianzhi was struck from the registers.
value.literal: When the prince was guilty, Jianzhi in the end sat for dismissal from the rolls.

value.zh: 帝幸遼東，召謇之檢校燕郡事。
value.en: On the Liaodong campaign the emperor summoned him to oversee Yan commandery.
value.literal: The emperor campaigned in Liaodong and summoned Jianzhi to inspect and manage Yan commandery affairs.

value.zh: 及帝班師，至燕郡，坐供頓不給，配戍嶺南。
value.en: On the return march he was convicted of failing to supply the army and was banished to Lingnan.
value.literal: When the emperor returned the army and reached Yan commandery, he sat because provisions were not supplied and was assigned to garrison in Lingnan.

value.zh: 卒于洭口，時年六十。
value.en: He died at Kuangkou at the age of sixty.
value.literal: He died at Kuangkou, aged sixty.

value.zh: 子威明。
value.en: His son was Weiming.
value.literal: His son Weiming.

value.zh: 族弟昂昂字千里。
value.en: His clansman Ang, styled Qianli.
value.literal: Clansman Ang—Ang styled Qianli.

value.zh: 父敏，有高名，好禮篤學，治家如官。
value.en: His father Min was renowned for propriety, learning, and running his household with official discipline.
value.literal: Father Min had a lofty reputation, loved rites and pursued learning deeply, and managed the household like an office.

value.zh: 仕周，曆職清顯。
value.en: Under the Zhou he held prominent offices.
value.literal: Serving Zhou, he held offices of clear prominence.

value.zh: 開皇初，為太子太保。
value.en: In early Kaihuang he became crown prince grand tutor.
value.literal: In early Kaihuang he was Crown Prince Grand Tutor.

value.zh: 昂有器識，幹局過人。
value.en: Ang had vision and administrative talent beyond ordinary men.
value.literal: Ang had capacity and insight; his organizing ability surpassed others.

value.zh: 周武帝時，為大內史，賜爵文城郡公，致位開府，當途用事，百僚皆出其下。
value.en: Under Zhou Emperor Wu he was grand secretariat director, Duke of Wencheng, pillar of state, and dominated the court.
value.literal: In Emperor Wu of Zhou's time he was Grand Secretariat Director, enfeoffed as Duke of Wencheng, reached Pillar of State, held power on the road, and all hundred officials were below him.

value.zh: 宣帝嗣位，稍被疏遠，然不離本職。
value.en: Under Emperor Xuan he was gradually sidelined but kept his post.
value.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded he was gradually distanced, yet did not leave his original post.

value.zh: 及高祖為丞相，深自結納。
value.en: When Gaozu became chancellor he allied himself closely with him.
value.literal: When Gaozu became Chancellor he deeply bound himself in alliance.

value.zh: 高祖大悅之，以為大宗伯。
value.en: Gaozu was delighted and appointed him grand director of the imperial clan.
value.literal: Gaozu was greatly pleased with him and made him Grand Director of the Imperial Clan.

value.zh: 昂受拜之日，遂得偏風，不能視事。
value.en: On the day of his appointment he suffered a stroke and could not take up his duties.
value.literal: On the day Ang received the appointment he immediately suffered partial wind-stroke and could not handle affairs.

value.zh: 高祖受禪，昂疾愈，加上開府，拜潞州刺史。
value.en: When Gaozu took the throne Ang recovered, was made upper pillar of state, and appointed prefect of Lu.
value.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication Ang's illness healed; he was added Upper Pillar of State and appointed Prefect of Lu.

value.zh: 昂見天下無事，可以勸學行禮，因上表曰：
value.en: Seeing the realm at peace, Ang memorialized that learning and ritual should be promoted:
value.literal: Ang saw that under heaven all was peaceful and one could encourage learning and practice rites; he therefore submitted a memorial saying:

value.zh: 趙逸 胡方回 胡叟 宋繇 張湛 宗欽 段承根 闞駰 劉昞 趙柔 索敞 陰仲達
value.en: Zhao Yi, and hu Fanghui, and hu Sou, and song Yao, and zhang Zhan, and zong Qin, and duan Chenggen, and yan Yin, and liu Bing, and zhao Rou, and suo Chang, and yin Zhongda
value.literal: Zhao Yi; Hu Fanghui; Hu Sou; Song Yao; Zhang Zhan; Zong Qin; Duan Chenggen; Yan Yin; Liu Bing; Zhao Rou; Suo Chang; Yin Zhongda

value.zh: 宗欽，字景若，金城人也。
value.en: Zong Qin, whose courtesy name was Jingruo, came from Jincheng.
value.literal: Zong Qin, courtesy name Jingruo, was a man of Jincheng.

value.zh: 父燮，字文友，呂光太常卿。
value.en: His father Xie, whose courtesy name was Wenyou, was Grand Master of Splendid Happiness under Lü Guang.
value.literal: His father Xie, courtesy name Wenyou, was Grand Master of Splendid Happiness under Lü Guang.

value.zh: 欽少而好學，有儒者之風，博綜羣言，聲著河右。
value.en: Qin from youth loved learning, had the air of a Confucian, ranged broadly through all schools of discourse, and his fame resounded west of the Yellow River.
value.literal: Qin from youth loved learning, had the air of a Confucian, ranged broadly through all schools of discourse, and his fame resounded in the lands west of the Yellow River.

value.zh: 仕沮渠蒙遜，為中書郎、世子洗馬。
value.en: Indeed, He served Juqu Mengxun as Secretariat Gentleman and Groom of the Heir Apparent.
value.literal: He served Juqu Mengxun as Secretariat Gentleman and Groom of the Heir Apparent.

value.zh: 欽上東宮侍臣箴曰：「恢恢玄古，悠悠生民。
value.en: Qin presented an Admonition for Eastern Palace Attendants, saying: "Vast, vast the dark antiquity, and long, long the living folk.
value.literal: Qin presented an Admonition for Eastern Palace Attendants, saying: "Vast, vast the dark antiquity; long, long the living folk.

value.zh: 五才迭用，經敍彝倫。
value.en: The five talents rotate in use, and the classics set out constant norms.
value.literal: The five talents rotate in use; the classics set out constant norms.

value.zh: 匡父維子，弼君伊臣。
value.en: To correct the father and sustain the son, to assist the ruler— ministers like Yi.
value.literal: To correct the father and sustain the son, to assist the ruler— ministers like Yi.

value.zh: 顛而能扶，屈而能申。
value.en: Upright when overturned yet able to support, and bent yet able to straighten.
value.literal: Upright when overturned yet able to support; bent yet able to straighten.

value.zh: 昔在上聖，妙鑒厥趣。
value.en: of old the highest sages subtly discerned this aim.
value.literal: Of old the highest sages subtly discerned this aim.

value.zh: 不曰我明，而乖其度。
value.en: Indeed, Not saying "I am enlightened" yet straying from its measure.
value.literal: Not saying "I am enlightened" yet straying from its measure.

value.zh: 不曰我新，而忽其故。
value.en: Indeed, Not saying "I am new" yet neglecting what is old.
value.literal: Not saying "I am new" yet neglecting what is old.

value.zh: 如彼在泉，臨深是懼。
value.en: like one beside a spring, in deep places he fears.
value.literal: Like one beside a spring, in deep places he fears.

value.zh: 如彼覆車，望途改步。
value.en: Indeed, [3] Like one beside an overturned cart, seeing the road he changes step.
value.literal: Like one beside an overturned cart, seeing the road he changes step.

value.zh: 是以令問宣流，英風遠布。
value.en: Therefore good repute spreads abroad, and heroic wind reaches far.
value.literal: Therefore good repute spreads abroad; heroic wind reaches far.

value.zh: 及於三季，道喪純遷。
value.en: Indeed, By the three degenerate ages the Way was lost and purity shifted.
value.literal: By the three degenerate ages the Way was lost and purity shifted.

value.zh: 桀起瓊臺，紂醊糟山。
value.en: Jie raised the Jade Terrace, and zhou piled the Mountain of Dregs.
value.literal: Jie raised the Jade Terrace; Zhou piled the Mountain of Dregs.

value.zh: 周滅妖姒，羿喪以田。
value.en: Zhou destroyed the evil Mo, and yi lost his state through fields.
value.literal: Zhou destroyed the evil Mo; Yi lost his state through fields.

value.zh: 險詖蔽其耳目，鄭衞陳於其前。
value.en: Peril and deceit blocked their ears and eyes, and zheng and Wei were set before them.
value.literal: Peril and deceit blocked their ears and eyes; Zheng and Wei were set before them.

value.zh: 怙才肆虐，異端是纏。
value.en: Relying on talent they acted wildly, and heterodox ways entangled them.
value.literal: Relying on talent they acted wildly; heterodox ways entangled them.

value.zh: 豈伊害身，厥胤殲焉。
value.en: did they only harm themselves? Their heirs were destroyed.
value.literal: Did they only harm themselves? Their heirs were destroyed.

value.zh: 茫茫禹跡，畫為九區。
value.en: Vast, vast the traces of Yu, and the land was drawn into nine regions.
value.literal: Vast, vast the traces of Yu; the land was drawn into nine regions.

value.zh: 昆蟲鳥獸，各有巢居。
value.en: insects, birds, and beasts— each had its nest and dwelling.
value.literal: Insects, birds, and beasts— each had its nest and dwelling.

value.zh: 雲歌唐后，垂橫美虞。
value.en: Cloud songs for the lord of Tang, and hanging banners praised Yu.
value.literal: Cloud songs for the lord of Tang; hanging banners praised Yu.

value.zh: 疏網改祝，殷道攸敷。
value.en: Loose nets changed the sacrifice, and the Yin Way was broadly spread.
value.literal: Loose nets changed the sacrifice; the Yin Way was broadly spread.

value.zh: 龍盤應德，隨蛇銜珠。
value.en: The dragon coiled responding to virtue, and the snake followed, holding a pearl.
value.literal: The dragon coiled responding to virtue; the snake followed, holding a pearl.

value.zh: 勿謂無心，識命不殊。
value.en: Do not say they were without mind, and they knew fate was not different.
value.literal: Do not say they were without mind; they knew fate was not different.

value.zh: 勿謂理絕，千載同符。
value.en: Do not say principle was cut off, and through a thousand ages the seal is the same.
value.literal: Do not say principle was cut off; through a thousand ages the seal is the same.

value.zh: 爰在子桓，靈數攸臻。
value.en: It came to the age of Zihuan, and the numinous tally was at hand.
value.literal: It came to the age of Zihuan; the numinous tally was at hand.

value.zh: 儀形徐阮，左右劉陳。
value.en: He took Xu and Ruan as models, and at his left and right Liu and Chen.
value.literal: He took Xu and Ruan as models; at his left and right Liu and Chen.

value.zh: 披文採友，叩典問津。
value.en: He spread writing and chose friends, and knocked at the canon and asked the ford.
value.literal: He spread writing and chose friends; knocked at the canon and asked the ford.

value.zh: 用能重離襲曜，魏鼎維新。
value.en: Thus he could renew the doubled radiance, and the Wei tripod was made new.
value.literal: Thus he could renew the doubled radiance; the Wei tripod was made new.

value.zh: 於昭儲后，運應玄籙。
value.en: Indeed, How glorious the Heir Apparent— his fortune matched the dark tally.
value.literal: How glorious the Heir Apparent— his fortune matched the dark tally.

value.zh: 夕惕乾乾，虛衿遠屬。
value.en: Evening vigil, morning diligence, and empty breast, far-reaching aim.
value.literal: Evening vigil, morning diligence; empty breast, far-reaching aim.

value.zh: 外撫幽荒，內懷焭獨。
value.en: Without he soothed the dark frontier, and within he cherished the orphaned and alone.
value.literal: Without he soothed the dark frontier; within he cherished the orphaned and alone.

value.zh: 猶懼思不逮遠，明不遐燭。
value.en: Still he feared his thought did not reach far, his clarity did not shine distant.
value.literal: Still he feared his thought did not reach far, his clarity did not shine distant.

value.zh: 君有諍臣，庭立謗木。
value.en: The ruler has remonstrating ministers, and in the court stands the slander-wood.
value.literal: The ruler has remonstrating ministers; in the court stands the slander-wood.

value.zh: 本枝克昌，永符天祿。
value.en: The root branches flourish, and forever matching heaven's blessing.
value.literal: The root branches flourish; forever matching heaven's blessing.

value.zh: 微臣作箴，敢告在僕。」
value.en: This humble servant composes an admonition— I dare report it to the attendant.".
value.literal: This humble servant composes an admonition— I dare report it to the attendant."

value.zh: 穆宗睿聖文惠孝皇帝諱恆，憲宗第三子也。
value.en: Emperor Muzong, posthumously honored as the Sagely Civil and Gracious Filial, bore the taboo name Heng and was the third son of Xianzong.
value.literal: Emperor Muzong, the Sagely Civil and Gracious Filial, taboo name Heng, was the third son of Xianzong.

value.zh: 母曰懿安皇太后郭氏。
value.en: His mother was Empress Dowager Yi'an, née Guo.
value.literal: His mother was Empress Dowager Yi'an of the Guo clan.

value.zh: 始封建安郡王，進封遂王，遙領彰義軍節度使。
value.en: He was first made Prince of Jian'an, then Prince of Sui, and served as Zhangyi military commissioner in absentia.
value.literal: He was first enfeoffed as Prince of Jian'an, then advanced to Prince of Sui, and held the post of Zhangyi army military commissioner in absentia.

value.zh: 元和七年，惠昭太子薨，左神策軍中尉吐突承璀欲立澧王惲，而惲母賤不當立，乃立遂王為皇太子。
value.en: In the seventh year of Yuanhe the heir apparent died; Tufa Chenghuan of the Left Divine Strategy Army sought to install Prince of Li Yun, but because Yun's mother was of humble status he could not be established, and the Prince of Sui was made heir apparent.
value.literal: In the seventh year of Yuanhe the Brightly Filial Heir Apparent died; the Left Divine Strategy Army eunuch-commander Tufa Chenghuan wished to install Prince of Li Yun, but Yun's mother was lowly and unfit to be established, so the Prince of Sui was established as heir apparent.

value.zh: 四月乙丑，昭義軍節度使劉從諫卒，其子稹自稱留後。
value.en: In the fourth month on yichou Liu Congjian of Zhaoyi died; his son Zhen declared himself acting commissioner.
value.literal: Fourth month, day yichou, the Zhaoyi military commissioner Liu Congjian died; his son Zhen styled himself acting commissioner.

value.zh: 五月甲午，震，東都廣運樓災。
value.en: In the fifth month on jiawu there was an earthquake and the Eastern Capital Broad Transport Tower burned.
value.literal: Fifth month, day jiawu, earthquake; the Eastern Capital Broad Transport Tower burned.

value.zh: 辛丑，成德軍節度使王元逵為北面招討澤潞使，魏博節度使何弘敬為東面招討澤潞使，及河中節度使陳夷行、河陽節度使王茂元、劉沔以討劉稹。
value.en: On xinchou Wang Yuankui of Chengde was made northern Ze-Lu campaign commissioner; He Hongjing of Weibo eastern commissioner; and Chen Yixing of Zhonghe, Wang Maoyuan of Heyang, and Liu Mian marched against Liu Zhen.
value.literal: On the day xinchou the Chengde military commissioner Wang Yuankui was made northern campaign commissioner against Ze and Lu; the Weibo military commissioner He Hongjing eastern campaign commissioner; together with the Zhonghe military commissioner Chen Yixing, Heyang military commissioner Wang Maoyuan, and Liu Mian to campaign against Liu Zhen.

value.zh: 戊申，翰林學士承旨、中書舍人崔鉉為中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。
value.en: On wushen Cui Xuan, Hanlin academician-in-chief and drafting officer, was appointed vice director of the Secretariat and chancellor de facto.
value.literal: On the day wushen the Hanlin academician-in-chief and Secretariat drafting officer Cui Xuan was made vice director of the Secretariat and chancellor de facto.

value.zh: 武寧軍節度使李彥佐為晉絳行營諸軍節度招討使。
value.en: Li Yanzhuo of Wuning was made Jin-He campaign military commissioner and commander.
value.literal: The Wuning military commissioner Li Yanzhuo was made Jin-He campaign military commissioner and campaign commander.

value.zh: 十月己巳，晉絳行營節度使石雄及劉稹戰于烏嶺，敗之。
value.en: In the tenth month on jisi Shi Xiong of the Jin-He campaign fought Liu Zhen at Black Ridge and defeated him.
value.literal: Tenth month, day jisi, the Jin-He campaign military commissioner Shi Xiong fought Liu Zhen at Black Ridge and defeated him.

value.zh: 壬午，日中月食太白。
value.en: On renwu at midday the moon eclipsed Venus.
value.literal: On the day renwu at midday the moon eclipsed Venus.

value.zh: 是月，党項羌寇鹽州。
value.en: That month the Tangut raided Yan prefecture.
value.literal: In that month the Tangut raided Yan prefecture.

value.zh: 八月乙未，昭義軍將郭誼殺劉稹以降。
value.en: In the eighth month on yiwei Zhaoyi officer Guo Yi killed Liu Zhen and surrendered.
value.literal: Eighth month, day yiwei, the Zhaoyi army officer Guo Yi killed Liu Zhen and surrendered.

value.zh: 戊戌，給復澤、潞、邢、洺、磁五州一歲，免太原、河陽及懷、陝、晉、絳四州秋稅。
value.en: On wushen Ze, Lu, Xing, Luo, and Ci received one year's tax remission; autumn tax was remitted in Taiyuan, Heyang, Huai, Shan, Jin, and Jiang.
value.literal: On the day wushen Ze, Lu, Xing, Luo, and Ci prefectures were granted tax remission for one year; autumn tax in Taiyuan, Heyang, and Huai, Shan, Jin, and Jiang prefectures was remitted.

value.zh: 戊申，李德裕為太尉。
value.en: On wushen Li Deyu was appointed grand preceptor.
value.literal: On the day wushen Li Deyu was made grand preceptor.

value.zh: 岑文本，字景仁，鄧州棘陽人。
value.en: Cen Wenben, whose courtesy name was Jingren, came from Jiyang in Deng Prefecture.
value.literal: Cen Wenben, courtesy name Jingren, was a native of Jiyang in Deng Prefecture.

value.zh: 祖善方，後梁吏部尚書，更家江陵。
value.en: His grandfather Shanfang had been Minister of Personnel under the Later Liang and resettled the family at Jiangling.
value.literal: His grandfather Shanfang was Minister of Personnel under Later Liang and moved the family to Jiangling.

value.zh: 父之象，仕隋為邯鄲令，坐為人訟，不得申。
value.en: His father Zhixiang served the Sui as magistrate of Handan but was sued by another party and could not vindicate himself.
value.literal: His father Zhixiang served the Sui as magistrate of Handan; he was implicated in a lawsuit brought against him and could not clear himself.

value.zh: 文本年十四，詣司隸理冤，辨對哀暢無所詘。
value.en: At fourteen Wenben went to the Censorate to plead his father's case and argued with such moving eloquence that no one could refute him.
value.literal: When Wenben was fourteen, he went to the Censorate to seek redress for the wrong; in debate he spoke movingly and fluently and was never worsted.

value.zh: 眾屬目，命作《蓮華賦》，文成，合臺嗟賞，遂得直。
value.en: All eyes were on him when he was told to write a "Rhapsody on the Lotus"; when he finished, the whole censorate marveled, and his father was cleared.
value.literal: The crowd fixed their eyes on him; he was ordered to compose the "Rhapsody on the Lotus"; when the text was finished, the whole bureau sighed in admiration, and he thereby obtained justice.

value.zh: 初，武德四年，太宗為天策上將軍，寇亂稍平，乃鄉儒，宮城西作文學館，收聘賢才，於是下教，以大行臺司勳郎中杜如晦、記室考功郎中房玄齡及于志寧、軍諮祭酒蘇世長、天策府記室薛收、文學褚亮姚思廉、太學博士陸德明孔穎達、主簿李玄道、天策倉曹參軍事李守素、王府記室參軍事虞世南、參軍事蔡允恭顏相時、著作郎攝記室許敬宗薛元敬、太學助教蓋文達、軍諮典簽蘇勖，並以本官為學士。
value.en: Early on, in the fourth year of Wude, the Prince of Qin held the title Grand General of Heavenly Strategy; as rebellion was partly subdued, he gathered Confucian scholars, built a Literature Hall west of the palace city, and recruited worthy men. He then issued an order naming Du Ruhui, Director of Meritorious Service in the Grand Secretariat; Fang Xuanling, Evaluation Director in the Secretariat; Yu Zhining; Su Shichang, Military Advisory Inspector; Xue Shou, Recorder of the Heavenly Strategy Office; the literary scholars Chu Liang and Yao Silian; the Imperial Academy erudites Lu Deming and Kong Yingda; chief clerk Li Xuandao; Li Shousu, storage clerk of the Heavenly Strategy Office; Yu Shinan, recording secretary of the princely establishment; staff members Cai Yungong and Yan Xiangshi; Xu Chongzong and Xue Yuanjing, Director of the Office of Compilation acting as recorder; Gai Wenda, assistant instructor of the Imperial Academy; and Su Xu, military advisory registrar -- all as academicians while keeping their original posts.
value.literal: Early, in the fourth year of Wude, the Prince of Qin was Grand General of Heavenly Strategy; as bandit chaos was somewhat pacified, he gathered Confucian scholars and built the Literature Hall west of the palace city to recruit worthy talent. Thereupon he issued an order appointing, while retaining their original offices, Du Ruhui, Director of Meritorious Service in the Grand Secretariat; Fang Xuanling, Evaluation Director in the Secretariat; Yu Zhining; Su Shichang, Military Advisory Inspector; Xue Shou, Recorder of the Heavenly Strategy Office; the Literary Scholars Chu Liang and Yao Silian; the Erudites of the Imperial Academy Lu Deming and Kong Yingda; Chief Clerk Li Xuandao; Li Shousu, Storage Clerk of the Heavenly Strategy Office; Yu Shinan, Recording Secretary of the Princely Establishment; the Staff Members Cai Yungong and Yan Xiangshi; Xu Chongzong and Xue Yuanjing, Director of the Office of Compilation acting as Recorder; Gai Wenda, Assistant Instructor of the Imperial Academy; and Su Xu, Military Advisory Registrar -- all as academicians in their existing posts.

value.zh: 七年，收卒，復召東虞州錄事參軍劉孝孫補之。
value.en: In the seventh year, after Shou died, Liu Xiaosun, recording officer of Dongyu Prefecture, was recalled to replace him.
value.literal: In the seventh year Shou died; Liu Xiaosun, Recording Officer of Dongyu Prefecture, was summoned again to fill the vacancy.

value.zh: 凡分三番遞宿於閤下，悉給珍膳。
value.en: They were divided into three shifts to lodge in rotation beneath the pavilion, and all were given fine meals.
value.literal: They were divided into three watches and took turns lodging beneath the pavilion; all were supplied with fine fare.

value.zh: 每暇日，訪以政事，討論墳籍，榷略前載，無常禮之間。
value.en: On free days he questioned them about government, debated the classics, and sifted former records, without the stiffness of ordinary court ritual.
value.literal: On each free day he consulted them on government affairs, discussed the classics, weighed and surveyed former records, without the constraints of ordinary ceremony.

value.zh: 命閻立本圖像，使亮為之贊，題名字爵裏，號「十八學士」，藏之書府，以章禮賢之重。
value.en: He had Yan Liben paint their portraits, Liang write the encomia, and their names, titles, and residences inscribed; the group was called the "Eighteen Academicians," kept in the library to show how highly he valued honoring talent.
value.literal: He ordered Yan Liben to paint their portraits, had Liang compose encomia for them, inscribed their names, titles, and residences, called them the "Eighteen Academicians," and stored the set in the library to display the weight he placed on honoring worthies.

value.zh: 方是時，在選中者，天下所慕問，謂之「登瀛洲」。
value.en: At that time those selected were the envy of the empire, and the post was called "Ascending to Yingzhou."
value.literal: At that time those chosen for it were admired and sought after throughout the realm, and the appointment was called "Ascending to Yingzhou."

value.zh: 附 劉孝孫劉孝孫者，荊州人。
value.en: Appended biography: Liu Xiaosun was a native of Jingzhou.
value.literal: Appended: Liu Xiaosun -- Liu Xiaosun was a man of Jingzhou.

value.zh: 祖貞，周石臺太守。
value.en: His grandfather Zhen served as administrator of Shitai under Northern Zhou.
value.literal: His grandfather Zhen was Administrator of Shitai under Zhou.

value.zh: 孝孫少知名。
value.en: Xiaosun was known even in youth.
value.literal: Xiaosun was known from youth.

value.zh: 大業末，為王世充弟杞王辯行臺郎中。
value.en: Near the end of Daye he served as director of the field secretariat for Bian, Prince of Qi, Wang Shichong's younger brother.
value.literal: At the end of Daye he served as Director of the Field Secretariat for Bian, Prince of Qi and younger brother of Wang Shichong.

value.zh: 辯降，眾引去，獨孝孫攀援號慟，送於郊。
value.en: When Bian surrendered, the others pulled away, but Xiaosun alone clung to him, wailing, and saw him off to the suburbs.
value.literal: When Bian surrendered, the crowd drew him away, but Xiaosun alone clung to him wailing in grief and escorted him to the outskirts.

value.zh: 貞觀六年，遷著作佐郎、吳王友。
value.en: In the sixth year of Zhenguan he became assistant director of the Office of Compilation and companion to the Prince of Wu.
value.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenguan he was transferred to Assistant Director of the Office of Compilation and Companion to the Prince of Wu.

value.zh: 歷諮議參軍。
value.en: He later served as advisory staff member.
value.literal: He served as Advisory Staff Member.

value.zh: 遷太子洗馬，未拜，卒。
value.en: He was appointed groom of the heir apparent but died before taking up the post.
value.literal: He was transferred to Groom of the Heir Apparent but died before assuming the post.

value.zh: 附 李玄道李玄道者，本隴西人。
value.en: Appended biography: Li Xuandao was originally from Longxi.
value.literal: Appended: Li Xuandao -- Li Xuandao was originally a man of Longxi.

value.zh: 世居鄭州。
value.en: His family had long lived in Zhengzhou.
value.literal: His family had long resided in Zhengzhou.

value.zh: 仕隋為齊王府屬。
value.en: Under Sui he served as an aide in the household of the Prince of Qi.
value.literal: He served Sui as an aide in the Princely Establishment of Qi.

value.zh: 李密據洛口，署記室。
value.en: When Li Mi held Luokou, Xuandao was made his recorder.
value.literal: When Li Mi held Luokou, [Xuandao] was appointed Recorder.

value.zh: 密敗，為王世充所執，眾懼不能寐，獨玄道曰：「死生有命，憂能了乎？」
value.en: When Mi fell, Xuandao was taken by Wang Shichong; the others were too afraid to sleep, but Xuandao alone said, "Life and death are fated -- can worry settle anything?"
value.literal: When Mi was defeated, [Xuandao] was seized by Wang Shichong; the crowd feared and could not sleep, but Xuandao alone said: "Life and death are ordained -- can worry finish the matter?"

value.zh: 寢甚安。
value.en: He slept soundly.
value.literal: He slept very peacefully.

value.zh: 及見世充，辭色不撓，釋縛，為著作佐郎。
value.en: When he was brought before Shichong, his words and bearing did not falter; Shichong freed him and made him assistant director of the Office of Compilation.
value.literal: When he was brought before Shichong, his words and demeanor did not waver; [Shichong] released his bonds and made him Assistant Director of the Office of Compilation.

value.zh: 東都平，為秦王府主簿。
value.en: After the Eastern Capital was pacified, he became chief clerk of the Prince of Qin's household.
value.literal: When the Eastern Capital was pacified, he became Chief Clerk of the Prince of Qin's establishment.

value.zh: 貞觀初，累遷給事中，姑臧縣男。
value.en: Early in Zhenguan he rose to supervising censor and was enfeoffed as Baron of Guzang County.
value.literal: Early in Zhenguan he was repeatedly promoted to Supervising Censor and enfeoffed as Baron of Guzang County.

value.zh: 出為幽州長史，佐都督王君廓，專持府事。
value.en: He was sent out as chief administrator of You Prefecture, assisting Area Commander Wang Junkuo and running the command's affairs himself.
value.literal: He was sent out as Chief Administrator of Youzhou, assisting the Area Commander Wang Junkuo and holding sole charge of the command's affairs.

value.zh: 君廓不法，每以義裁糾之。
value.en: Junkuo broke the law, and Xuandao repeatedly corrected him on grounds of principle.
value.literal: Junkuo acted unlawfully, and [Xuandao] repeatedly checked him by right principle.

value.zh: 嘗遺玄道婢，乃良家子為所掠，遣去不納，由是始隙。
value.en: Once Junkuo sent Xuandao a maidservant who turned out to be a good family's daughter he had seized; Xuandao sent her back and refused the gift, and from that their breach began.
value.literal: Once [Junkuo] sent Xuandao a maidservant who was in fact a respectable family's daughter whom he had seized; Xuandao sent her away and would not accept her, and from this their rift began.

value.zh: 君廓入朝，玄道寓書房玄齡，玄齡本甥也。
value.en: When Junkuo went to court, Xuandao was staying with Fang Xuanling, who was his nephew.
value.literal: Junkuo went to court; Xuandao was lodging at the house of Fang Xuanling -- Xuanling was his nephew by birth.

value.zh: 君廓發其書，不識草字，疑以謀己，遂反。
value.en: Junkuo opened the letter, could not decipher the cursive hand, suspected a plot against him, and rose in rebellion.
value.literal: Junkuo opened the letter, could not read cursive script, suspected a plot against himself, and rebelled.

value.zh: 坐是流巂州，未幾，擢常州刺史，風績清簡，下詔褒美，賜繒帛。
value.en: For this Xuandao was banished to Juan Prefecture; soon after he was promoted to prefect of Changzhou, where his rule was clear and spare; the throne issued a decree of praise and granted him silk.
value.literal: For this [Xuandao] was exiled to Juan Prefecture; before long he was promoted to prefect of Changzhou; his governance was clear and plain; an edict praised him and granted silk.

value.zh: 久之，致仕，加銀青光祿大夫，以祿歸第，卒。
value.en: In time he retired, was made Silver Gleaming Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, went home on his stipend, and died.
value.literal: After a long time he retired; was given the title Silver Gleaming Grand Master for Splendid Happiness; returned home on his salary; and died.

value.zh: 附 李守素李守素者，趙州人。
value.en: Appendix: Li Shousu. Li Shousu came from Zhao Prefecture.
value.literal: Appendix: Li Shousu. Li Shousu was a man of Zhao Prefecture.

value.zh: 王世充平，召署天策府倉曹參軍，通氏姓學，世號「肉譜」。
value.en: After Wang Shichong was subdued, Li was summoned and made warehouse clerk in the Celestial Stratagem Office; expert in clan and surname lore, his age called him the "Meat Genealogy."
value.literal: When Wang Shichong was pacified, [Li] was summoned and appointed Warehouse Clerk in the Celestial Stratagem Office; versed in the study of surnames and clans, the age styled him the "Meat Genealogy."
